records.excerpt: ChatGPT release notes | OpenAI Help Center OpenAI Support ChatGPT release notes Review the latest updates and release notes for ChatGPT. Updated: 5 days ago November 23, 2026 GPT-6.2, now in the chat tab We’re rolling out a version of GPT-6.2, optimized for the chat tab, for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers. It’s better at handling more complex requests that involve following detailed instructions or finding information online. If you’re comparing hotels for a weekend trip, it can help you weigh trade-offs like price and location and recommend the one that best fits your priorities. It’s also better at knowing when to follow up. For example, if you ask whether something is on sale, ChatGPT can offer to let you know when the price drops. Better at understanding images and following instructions GPT‑6.2 is better at answering questions about the images you share. In our tests in the Chat tab, it scored 71.7% on image understanding, up from 47.4% for GPT‑6. On especially challenging prompts, GPT-6.2 followed instructions 78.1% of the time, up from 62.5% for GPT-6. At the lowest reasoning setting we tested, GPT‑6.2 scored 65% on an internal evaluation of expert-level tasks, up from 52% for GPT‑6. GPT‑6.2 was also better at finding answers to difficult questions on the web. On an internal version of BrowseComp, it outperformed GPT‑6 at all four reasoning settings. At Extra high, GPT‑6.2 scored about 10 percentage points higher (64.5% vs. 54.4%). Deploying GPT-6.2 safely GPT‑6.2 shows significantly improved performance on our teen safety evaluations, with the largest gains in emotional reliance, disordered eating, and age-restricted goods, services, and dangerous activities. In evaluations of policy compliance in challenging conversations, responses met our safety policies 91–94% of the time, up from 77–80% for GPT‑6. Read more in our system card . Availability GPT‑6.2 starts rolling out globally to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers today in the Chat tab. Enterprise availability depends on workplace admin settings. GPT‑6.2 in ChatGPT is powered by a version of GPT‑6.2 Sol for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers, and is tuned for everyday conversation. This update applies to the Chat experience in ChatGPT. The models powering Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release. November 20, 2026 ChatGPT Space is rolling out to Plus Starting today, ChatGPT Space is rolling out globally to Plus users ages 18 and older. In Space, you can create interactive pages and presentations with ChatGPT, then invite other people with Space access to build on them with you. You can also set pages and slides to automatically update based on your connected apps and tools. Try making a to-do list that updates itself, a study guide with a 3D model you can explore, or a project plan that stays current with decisions from Slack. Tag ChatGPT in a comment to ask for changes. If you have a dot, you can invite it to collaborate, too. To open a shared page or presentation, you need permission to view it and must be signed in to a Plus, Pro, Business, or Enterprise account with Space access. People on Free can’t open shared pages or presentations. Public links aren’t available. To get started, open Space in the sidebar. It replaces Library and is your new home for pages, slides, images, and uploaded files. Use Space on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android to create and edit pages. November 19, 2026 New mobile experience for ChatGPT We’re rolling out a new experience for the ChatGPT mobile app that makes it easier to get to your favorite features and discover more of what you can do. Your dot has its own tab, and you can pin favorites like Codex, Projects, and Images to the tab bar. We’re starting with ChatGPT Pro users who are 18 or older in regions where dots are available. This rollout excludes the European Economic Area (including the EU), the UK, Switzerland, and Korea. A small group of eligible Plus users will also see the new experience. Some eligible Pro users will see the new experience by default. If New ChatGPT design appears in Settings , you can turn it on or off there. Learn more about the new experience in the ChatGPT mobile app . Health on Android, desktop, dots and sites Starting today, Health is rolling out to more of the places you use ChatGPT, including the desktop app, dots, sites, and Android, with support for Health Connect. Connect your health and fitness information with Android Health Connect to explore patterns in your sleep, activity, and more. Get proactive suggestions from your dot, like another time for a workout when a meeting gets in the way or a reminder about preventive care options based on your connected medical records. Use the desktop app to build a site to track your marathon training, with your runs and progress toward your training plan in one place. To get started, update to the latest ChatGPT app and select Health in the sidebar. If it isn’t listed, find Health in the Explore menu . This update is rolling out gradually, so it may not be available for your account yet. Health is available to Free, Go, Plus, and Pro users in the U.S. Dots are currently available to Pro users. See: Getting started with your dot . Learn more about Health in ChatGPT . November 18, 2026 Live Dictation in ChatGPT Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable. With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. Tap or click on the waveform to show or hide text as you go. We’ve also removed the 10-minute recording limit. Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web, and the desktop app. Learn more about voice dictation . Accounting workflows in ChatGPT The Accounting plugin helps you reconcile transactions, draft invoice entries, and prepare month-end reports from your records and templates. Open the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS or Windows, set up computer use , and open the Accounting plugin listing. Select Install plugin if it’s available for your plan and workspace. In Enterprise workspaces, an admin must approve Accounting before members can install it. November 17, 2026 GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol in ChatGPT Work and Codex We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Astra is our frontier model for complex work across research, software development, and other professional fields. Sol combines strong reasoning with speed and efficiency for a wide range of everyday tasks. Both models are available in preview in Work and Codex desktop. On Plus or Pro, choose either model in the Work model picker or the Codex model selector . In a managed workspace, the models you see depend on your seat and workspace settings. Regular Chat keeps its existing model choices . November 16, 2026 Clinical search and plugins for ChatGPT for Clinicians We’ve improved clinical search in ChatGPT for Clinicians, with updates to how ChatGPT finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence. Healthcare plugins also let you connect supported tools to ChatGPT. Plugin availability and requirements vary. For details, see: ChatGPT for Clinicians . November 13, 2026 Introducing ChatGPT Wallet ChatGPT Wallet helps your dot go from finding what you need to making a purchase on your behalf. Whether you’re shopping for a new sweater or booking a hotel, you can ask your dot to help and use Wallet when it’s time to check out. Save an eligible card once, then approve purchases without entering your payment details again. Before your dot pays, you review the merchant, items, total, and selected card, then authorize the purchase using biometrics such as Face ID or Touch ID. Wallet provides a substitute payment credential for checkout, keeping your actual card details hidden from the agent and business. records.label: Business Insider OpenAI and Codex analysis
records.title: ChatGPT is no longer OpenAI's endgame. This is why.
records.excerpt: ChatGPT may no longer be OpenAI's most important product as the company chases stickier, higher-margin businesses. The next battle in AI will have less to do with model quality and more to do with customer lock-in. For the past few years, OpenAI and Anthropic have competed relentlessly on model performance. But according to Samuel Colvin, CEO of AI startup Pydantic, the economics are changing. "A year ago, what they cared about was revenue," Colvin told me recently. "Now, when one assumes they're both trying to IPO, their profit margin becomes really important." The problem is that competing solely on model quality is expensive. Frontier labs must spend billions training ever-better models that are soon emulated. That's not a great recipe for durable profits. Instead, Colvin believes OpenAI and Anthropic are increasingly focused on building products that are harder for customers to leave. "They are doing their very best to find ways of locking people in that are not related to model quality," he said. "That's where I think Claude Code and Codex and all that work is coming from." AI coding services already look like better businesses than chatbots. Developers can quickly consume huge numbers of tokens while running Claude Code or Codex on complex projects, generating far more usage (and revenue) than a typical chat session. These tools could also become exceptionally sticky. Claude Code and Codex help companies generate software at unprecedented speed, creating codebases that grow beyond what human developers can realistically manage. Companies could find themselves dependent on the same AI tools to maintain, update, and understand the software those tools helped create. That may help explain why Anthropic and OpenAI are racing to turn Claude Code and Codex into broader AI-powered work platforms rather than standalone coding products. Anthropic is pushing in this direction with Cowork, while OpenAI is planning to merge Codex into ChatGPT. The catch is that customers are moving the other way. Consider Walmart's home-grown coding assistant, Code Puppy. It's designed to avoid dependence on any single AI provider, and give the retail giant more control over its codebase. The system can switch between models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others, helping Walmart control costs and reduce vendor lock-in. That's the tension increasingly shaping the AI market. OpenAI and Anthropic want sticky, high-margin products that keep customers inside their ecosystems. Enterprise buyers want flexibility, portability, and lower token bills. The winners of the next phase of AI may be the companies that best navigate this conflict. Sign up for BI's Tech Memo newsletter here. Reach out to me via email at abarr@businessinsider.com.

records.excerpt: Artificial Intelligence | The Verge Skip to main content The homepage The homepage Navigation Drawer Login / Sign Up Subscribe AI Artificial intelligence is more a part of our lives than ever before. While some might call it hype and compare it to NFTs or 3D TVs, generative AI is causing a sea change in nearly every part of the technology industry. OpenAI’s ChatGPT is still the best-known AI chatbot around, but with Google pushing Gemini, Microsoft building Copilot, and Apple adding its Intelligence to Siri, AI is probably going to be in the spotlight for a very long time. At The Verge, we’re exploring what might be possible with AI — and a lot of the bad stuff AI does, too. RELATED / Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun You can have a good time brewing up widgets — as long as you don’t expect too much.﻿ Allison Johnson Nov 27 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats A bipartisan coalition of AGs say Character.AI is planning to sell the personal data of minors to the highest bidder. Terrence O'Brien Nov 26 Latest In AI Sean Hollister Nov 27 Will future generations shove earbuds into their mouths to avoid the embarrassment of visibly talking to AI? The InvisiSpeech is the work of Aarhus doctoral student Yijing Jiang and a team spanning ETH Zürich and Penn State; it claims to be “the first silent speech interface that is designed for truly invisible interaction through an intraoral device.” In an early 15-person study , “subtle tongue movements” were enough to help Siri recognize 50 basic commands like “How’s the stock market doing?” Dominic Preston Nov 27 Nvidia’s most powerful chips made it into Chinese data centers linked to Megaspeed. Bloomberg reports that Blackwell GB200 and GB300 chips — which weren’t approved for export to China — have been installed in at least two data centers with links to Megaspeed, Alice Huang’s former company , now blacklisted by the US . At this point that’s no great surprise, but it wasn’t meant to be possible. Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang [ Bloomberg ] Dominic Preston Nov 26 Florida man imprisoned for using AI to impersonate a streamer in a crypto scam. That’s gotta complete someone’s bingo card. David Anthony Sanchez used fake accounts and an AI voice recording to impersonate streamer N3on and steal $260,000 in crypto through endorsement of a memecoin. As Aftermath points out, N3on was a fitting target — he’d previously used AI to create fake streams of himself, and “starred” in an AI movie . Port St. Lucie Man Sentenced to 47 Months in Prison for Using AI to Impersonate Popular Streamer in $260,000 in Cryptocurrency Fraud Scheme [ United States Attorney’s Office ] Dominic Preston Nov 26 Anthropic has started paying out its copyright settlement to authors. Novelist Courtney Milan says she’s already received her part of Anthropic’s $1.5 billion payout , which it agreed to last year to settle a class-action suit from authors. The full payout should work out to around $3,000 per book, but part of that is still to come early next year . Dominic Preston Nov 26 Now Nvidia’s stopped sending chips to Southeast Asia too. The company already said it had stopped selling AI chips to China , and now the Financial Times reports it’s halted shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, ‌Thailand, and Indonesia too. It follows tighter US restrictions introduced last week, intended to limit Chinese access to AI compute via overseas data centers. Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia [ Financial Times ] Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future Charles Pulliam-Moore Nov 25 Stevie Bonifield Nov 25 Ubuntu is working on an AI launcher for its Linux desktop. Canonical’s Didier Roche shared a preview screenshot of the new AI feature coming in January, showing a prompt box on an Ubuntu homescreen. Roche describes it as “a unified, keyboard and speech-friendly entry point that bridges your apps, your local context, and smart assistance only when you explicitly ask for it.” Image: Canonical Terrence O'Brien Nov 25 Dario Amodei clarifies he doesn’t believe we should “surrender free will to AI.” The Anthropic CEO is pushing back against insinuations by other AI execs, published in Axios , that he and his company believe we should surrender free will to AI. He did so in a totally normal 1,000-word X post , saying he’s been “vocal and consistent” that it would “be a terrible idea.” Terrence O'Brien Nov 25 Etsy clarified its AI training policy, but sellers still aren’t happy. When the platform updated its terms of service to allow it to train AI models on user listings, sellers revolted . On Monday, the company posted updated terms with clarifying language, but it doesn’t seem to have quelled the backlash , and many still plan to leave Etsy. CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said in a blog post : “We will not use your content to create copycat versions of the work you sell on Etsy. We use your content to build tools that do things like help buyers find your items, help you run your shop, improve customer support, promote your work, and keep our marketplace safe.” Terrence O'Brien Nov 25 New York bans AI chatbot toys for kids. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill putting a five-year pause on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of AI chatbot toys, including “talking stuffed animals, dolls and robots that use the internet to hold conversations with kids.” This comes just one month after the state also restricted how chatbots could interact with minors. Governor Hochul Signs Five-Year Ban on AI Chatbot Toys [ Governor Kathy Hochul ] FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space Emma Roth Nov 25 Elizabeth Lopatto Nov 25 Impunity: maybe not good for business? Dan Davies, author of Lying for Money and The Unaccountability Machine , weighs in on Jensen Huang’s return, and the downside of elite impunity : “Huang may be a lot more damaged as a manager and businessperson than people think; I also notice that OpenAI has never really recovered its lead since it did the same ‘LOL, nothing matters’ trick with Sam Altman.“ the curse of impunity [ back of mind ] Emma Roth Nov 25 OpenAI is combining ChatGPT and Codex usage limits. As OpenAI gets ready to fold its “chat” and “work” tabs into one interface, the company will begin sharing usage limits between ChatGPT and Codex for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers in December. OpenAI says it expects “most users won’t need to wait for their usage to reset more often than they do now.” Understanding ChatGPT and Codex usage limits | OpenAI Help Center [ OpenAI Help Center ] Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case Emma Roth Nov 25 David Pierce Nov 25 Today’s Vergecast: Big Tech is ready to spend even bigger to win in 2028. The crypto and AI industries both spent huge on the 2026 US midterm elections. They’ll tell you otherwise, but they both lost big . Molly White, who writes Citation Needed and maintains the Tech Influence Watch spending tracker, joins the show to explain why AI and crypto couldn’t buy a win — and why they’re ready to spend even bigger in two years. Watch | Listen | Get ad-free Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block Emma Roth Nov 25 Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths? Companies like Akai have decided to embrace the modding community rather than resist vibe coders. Terrence O'Brien Nov 25 Dominic Preston Nov 25 EA Sports FC is resurrecting a deceased commentator with AI. Former BBC Sports commentator John Motson will be added to the 2027 edition of the game tomorrow despite dying in 2023. He was the first ever commentator in the series, back in Fifa 96 . His widow and son say they’ve approved the digital revival, which was achieved with a mix of archival recordings and generative AI. records.title: アンソロピックが公開価格割れ、OpenAI上場観測が後退 2027年6月までの発表確率28%に低下
records.excerpt: 予測市場カルシのトレーダーらは現在、OpenAIが2027年6月までに正式にIPOを発表する確率を約28%と見積もっており、11月上旬の50%超から低下した。2027年10月まででも確率はほぼ50%と五分五分にとどまる。この見直しは、競合アンソロピックの低調な上場初日を受けたものだ。同社株は火曜日に81.91ドルで引け、IPO価格の83ドルを下回り、上場初日の高値から約30%下落した。暗号資産プラットフォームのハイパーリキッドでOpenAIに連動する無期限先物は10月上旬から30%超下落。OpenAIは現在の資金調達目標を1.25兆ドル評価で300億ドルから200億ドル（約3.2兆円）に引き下げた。一方、キャシー・ウッド氏率いるアークのファンドはアンソロピック株をさらに75万1,710株買い増した。 アンソロピックの株価が公開価格を下回って取引され、AI関連取引の巻き戻しが続く中、予測市場プラットフォームのカルシ（Kalshi）の賭け手らは、OpenAIが2027年半ばまでに正式に上場を発表する確率を大幅に引き下げた。CNBCによると、市場が織り込む確率は今週約28%まで低下し、11月上旬の50%超から下がった。 期間を延ばしても市場の見方は割れている。カルシのトレーダーらは、2027年10月までに正式なIPO発表がある確率を約50%と五分五分に見ている。 これらの契約は「発表」を狭く定義して決済される。米証券取引委員会（SEC）がS-1登録届出書を有効と宣言するか、IPO価格が決定するか、取引所がティッカーシンボルを割り当てた場合のいずれかだ。取引が開始されていなくても支払いが発生し、判定は報道に基づく。 OpenAIは6月に非公開で上場申請を行い、最初の正式な一歩を踏み出した。しかし9月に公開されたフォーチュン誌のインタビューで、最高経営責任者（CEO）のサム・アルトマン氏は、人工知能の安全性への懸念が高まる中、2026年の上場を否定した。アルトマン氏は、重要な安全上の問題が未解決のまま市場に急ぐべきではないとの考えを示している。 アンソロピック（ANT）からのシグナルは無視しがたい。OpenAIの競合である同社は11月19日に上場し、初値は111.50ドルと公開価格83ドルを約34%上回った。初日は17%上昇したが、その後は反転した。火曜日は81.91ドルで引け、公開価格を下回り、上場初日の日中高値から約30%低い水準となった。 別途開示された情報によると、CEOのダリオ・アモデイ氏が2.8億ドル（約450億円）超相当の337万株超を売却しており、圧力が加わった。ただしこれらの株式は公開市場での売却ではなく、上場の一環としてIPOの引受会社に渡ったものだ。また、アンソロピックとOpenAIの両社の従業員が、高度なモデルが制御不能なほど強力になる可能性があると警鐘を鳴らしているとの報道も浮上した。 デリバティブ市場も同様の状況を示している。暗号資産プラットフォームのハイパーリキッド（Hyperliquid）でOpenAIに連動する無期限先物契約は、10月上旬の高値から30%超下落した。 非公開市場側では、OpenAIは1.25兆ドル（約199兆円）の評価額で資金調達を進めているが、先月下旬に今回のラウンドの目標額を300億ドル（約4.8兆円）から200億ドル（約3.2兆円）に引き下げた。 カルシが示すOpenAIの正式IPO発表確率 2027年6月まで 約28%（11月上旬は50%超） 2027年10月まで 約50% 注：カルシは、S-1の有効化、IPO価格の決定、ティッカーシンボルの割り当てのいずれかを発表とみなす。 すべての投資家が後退しているわけではない。キャシー・ウッド氏率いるアークのファンドは火曜日、アンソロピック株をさらに75万1,710株買い増した。上場後最初の2取引日で取得した164万株に追加した形だ。アークはAI関連の売りを買い場と位置づけており、チーフ・フューチャリストのブレット・ウィントン氏は、OpenAIとアンソロピックが規模拡大に伴い、計算能力1ギガワット当たりの収益を増やしていると主張する。同社は両社の合計年換算収益が約1,400億ドル（約22.3兆円）に達したと推計している。 アンソロピックに対する売り手側の評価も前向きだ。TipRanksによると、9件の「買い」と1件の「保有」で構成される「強い買い」のコンセンサスが形成されており、平均目標株価は133.89ドルで、火曜日の終値から約63.5%の上昇余地を示唆する。 この問題の影響は単一の上場にとどまらない。OpenAIの公開企業への転換は、個人投資家と機関投資家が現在の評価額でAIインフラへの資金供給を続けるかどうかを試す最大の試金石となる。上場が延期されたり規模が縮小されたりすれば、非公開市場の評価額や、継続的な拡大を織り込んできたサプライチェーンに波及する可能性がある。現時点で予測市場は拒否ではなく忍耐を織り込んでいる。トレーダーらは依然として上場を予想しているが、数週間前より遅い時期を見込んでいる。
records.evidence: Google News RSSで「アンソロピックが公開価格割れ、OpenAI上場観測が後退 2027年6月までの発表確率28%に低下」を確認し、配信元ページhttps://finance.biggo.jp/news/f44100e9-df53-4078-af9f-1efe62a908bbを特定した。本文抽出: 予測市場カルシのトレーダーらは現在、OpenAIが2027年6月までに正式にIPOを発表する確率を約28%と見積もっており、11月上旬の50%超から低下した。2027年10月まででも確率はほぼ50%と五分五分にとどまる。この見直しは、競合アンソロピックの低調な上場初日を受けたものだ。同社株は火曜日に81.91ドルで引け、IPO価格の83ドルを下回り、上場初日の高値から約30%下落した。暗号資産プラットフォームのハイパーリキッドでOpenAIに連動する無期限先物は10月上旬から30%超下落。OpenAIは現在の資金調達目標を1.25兆ドル評価で300億ドルから200億ドル（約3.2兆円）に引き下げた。一方、キャシー・ウッド氏率いるアークのファンドはアンソロピック株をさらに75万1,710株買い増した。 アンソロピックの株価が公開価格を下回って取引され、AI関連取引の巻き戻しが続く中、予測市場プラットフォームのカルシ（Kalshi）の賭け手らは、OpenAIが2027年半ばまでに正式に上場を発表する確率を大幅に引き下げた。CNBCによると、市場が織り込む確率は今週約28%まで低下し、11月上旬の50%超から下がった。 期間を延ばしても市場の見方は割れている。カルシのトレーダーらは、2027年10月までに正式なIPO発表がある確率を約50%と五分五分に見ている。 これらの契約は「発表」を狭く定義して決済される。米証券取引委員会（SEC）がS-1登録届出書を有効と宣言するか、IPO価格が決定するか、取引所がティッカーシンボルを割り当てた場合のいずれかだ。取引が開始されていなくても支払い

Create a free account Menu Crypto sections Bitcoin Ethereum Altcoins DeFi Stablecoins Regulation Security Create account Log in Español Prediction markets push OpenAI IPO expectations to 2027 FoxTPNL / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0) Kalshi traders now give OpenAI only a 28% chance of announcing an IPO by June 2027 after Anthropic's rough public debut by Estefano Gomez Wed 25 Nov 2026 · 12:25 EST · 3 min read In Prediction Markets Share Follow on Google A month ago, the crowd on Kalshi thought an OpenAI IPO announcement was more likely than not by mid-2027. Now traders on the prediction market put the odds at roughly 28%. The drop came in a hurry. The odds of the ChatGPT maker announcing a public offering by June 2027 were above 50% earlier this month. Then Anthropic went public, and the vibes went sideways. What the markets are pricing Traders currently price a 28% chance that OpenAI announces an IPO by June 1, 2027. The odds climb to 48% for an announcement before July 1, 2027, and to 61% before August 1, 2027. There is real money behind these guesses. Volume on Kalshi’s OpenAI IPO date contracts tops $1.46 million, and the activity points to traders expecting confirmation before October 2027. Polymarket, a rival prediction market, tells a similar story. Its contracts give OpenAI only 1-2% odds of listing in 2026, with probability leaning toward a 2027 announcement. Create a free account The Anthropic effect The catalyst was Anthropic’s public market debut on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026. It did not go the way anyone selling shares would have scripted. Anthropic shares opened at $111.50. Within days, they slipped below the $83 IPO price, trading as low as $75-78, with a range of $75-82 in the period that followed. See what prediction markets are pricing into the day's biggest stories. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The timing made it worse. Anthropic’s slide coincided with a broader tech sell-off, which the research ties to growing concern about AI valuations. For OpenAI, Anthropic is the closest possible comparable. Both build frontier AI models, both burn significant capital, and both have been valued in private markets on expectations of enormous future growth. Background: OpenAI’s road to the public markets OpenAI’s IPO chatter is not new. The company confidentially filed an S-1, the registration document required before a US public offering, around June 8, 2026. Even then, the research indicates the IPO timeline had begun shifting from 2026 toward 2027 by late June. Prediction markets largely followed that drift, which is why the 2026 listing odds on Polymarket now sit in low single digits. What changed this month is not the year. It is the confidence within that year. Traders had been treating the first half of 2027 as a reasonable bet, and Anthropic’s debut knocked that conviction down sharply. What this means The bigger signal is about AI valuations in general. Private funding rounds can set eye-watering price tags, but public markets get the final vote. Anthropic’s trading below its offering price is a reminder that enthusiasm in a funding round does not automatically translate into demand from public buyers. The episode also highlights how prediction markets have become a fast-reacting barometer for corporate events. Odds on Kalshi moved from above 50% to roughly 28% within weeks. With more than $1.46 million in volume on the OpenAI date contracts alone, these markets are increasingly a place where sentiment on private companies gets expressed in real time. That said, prediction market odds reflect what traders believe, not what OpenAI has decided. The company has not publicly committed to a date. What to watch next: Anthropic’s share price relative to its $83 offering level, the direction of the broader tech sell-off, and any movement in the June and July 2027 Kalshi contracts. They are losing money faster than most companies ever earn it. Anthropic reported a net loss of $104 billion for the first three quarters of 2026, on revenue of $33.2 billion. OpenAI generated around $10 billion in revenue in Q3 2026 and posted adjusted operating losses of $10.9 billion over the same stretch. New financial disclosures from both firms have increased Wall Street’s scrutiny of AI valuations. Arthur Hayes, the former BitMEX executive better known for his crypto market essays, has a blunt diagnosis: the closed-source AI labs may end up as government contractors. The numbers behind the hype Start with Anthropic, which went public in mid-November 2026. The IPO valued the company at approximately $1.5 trillion, a figure usually reserved for firms that have spent decades printing profits. The debut did not go entirely to plan. Shares declined shortly after opening, a disappointing start for one of the most anticipated tech listings. The $104 billion loss needs context. Of that total, $94.3 billion came from non-cash adjustments tied to financing instruments. Most of the loss is the accounting treatment of how the company raised money. Its roughly $10 billion in Q3 2026 revenue was 50% sequential growth. Adjusted operating losses still hit $10.9 billion in that quarter alone. The compute bill and the pricing problem The core issue is cost structure. Training and running frontier AI models requires enormous fixed investments in compute and infrastructure. Anthropic alone has committed more than $900 billion in leases and purchases, with obligations stretching through 2045. That is a two-decade bet that demand for premium AI will keep growing at prices high enough to cover the bill. Leading US models charge between $2 and $40 per million tokens. Competitors are charging much less. Open-source models and Chinese AI labs offer capable alternatives at a fraction of the cost. Why Arthur Hayes thinks Washington is the endgame Hayes has questioned the AI labs’ long-term sustainability for some time. In October 2026, he asked whether these companies could survive without US government support. His argument rests on two pressures. First, cheap open-source models limit how much the closed labs can charge. Second, businesses are wary of sharing their proprietary data with outside AI providers, which caps how deeply enterprise customers are willing to commit. With a company squeezed from both sides like that, Hayes suggests the closed-source labs may have no viable future under current market conditions. The implied alternative is a shift toward government-backed financing or something like a utility model, with Washington as a major customer and backstop. To be precise: Hayes is making a forecast. He is not reporting a plan. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI has announced a pivot to government contracting as a core business. What this means for investors and the AI trade For public market investors, Anthropic’s listing turns an abstract debate into a daily price signal. Every quarterly report will now be measured against a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion, and the early share price decline suggests some buyers are already skeptical. The $900 billion-plus commitment is the main risk to watch. Those obligations are locked in regardless of what happens to token prices. If open-source alternatives keep closing the quality gap, Anthropic could be paying premium infrastructure costs to sell an increasingly commoditized product. Hayes’s government-contractor thesis is one possible outcome. Utility-like businesses tend to have stable revenue but limited upside, a very different profile from the one used to justify trillion-dollar valuations. records.title: Facing Legal Pressure And Industry Alarm, OpenAI And Meta Push For AI Development Guardrails As Anthropic (NYSE: ANT) IPO Fuels Market Frenzy
records.excerpt: A California lawsuit alleging OpenAI knowingly built AI models without adequate safeguards has intensified an already heated debate about who should set the A California lawsuit alleging OpenAI knowingly built AI models without adequate safeguards has intensified an already heated debate about who should set the boundaries of artificial intelligence development. The state’s attorney general cited the July Hugging Face attack among other claims, framing OpenAI as a company that prioritized capability over public safety. Against that legal backdrop, OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a blog post proposing that major AI developers agree on shared capability thresholds they would collectively pledge not to cross. Pachocki suggested that “perplexity,” a technical measure of how accurately a model predicts the next token in a sequence, could serve as a common industry benchmark for gauging model power. Lower perplexity scores indicate stronger predictive performance, and Pachocki argued the metric could anchor enforceable commitments across competing labs. “I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone,” Pachocki wrote. Pachocki also flagged 2027 as a potential inflection point, warning that AI systems could begin accelerating their own training methods within that timeframe, raising the urgency of agreeing on limits now. CEO Sam Altman amplified the proposal on X, writing: “We are providing a lot of transparency into our pretraining progress and hope we can agree as a field to common limits. I think that would be very wise and help ensure safety and control.” Meta Platforms’ Alexandr Wang echoed the concern from a different angle, arguing that AI models have largely cleared the intelligence barrier and will soon automate research into their own improvement, becoming “clearly superhuman at improving themselves.” Wang warned that rapid self-improvement cycles could extend into biology, cybersecurity, and weapons research, raising risks that exceed humanity’s current ability to manage them. His warning carried a stark conclusion: “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” with Wang calling for immediate advances in safety, alignment, and security infrastructure. The proposals from both companies arrive just as Anthropic (NYSE: ANT) completed a blockbuster public offering that sent its stock up 17% on its first trading day before gains faded in subsequent sessions. ANT edged higher in overnight trading amid a broader relief rally across the tech sector, and retail sentiment on Stocktwits held at “extremely bullish,” a reading that has not shifted since the IPO. One retail trader captured the mood around ANT bluntly, writing: “$ANT the Riemann hypothesis cracking machine isn’t going anywhere. Their proprietary tech and know-how is what’s valuable, not hardware. Given that they’re hardware constrained and are still busting centuries old proofs is actually more bullish, their models do most of the lifting.” By contrast, Stocktwits sentiment for Meta stood at “bearish,” while OpenAI’s reading was “bullish,” reflecting divergent investor views even as the two companies align on the need for industry-wide AI limits. records.excerpt: Title: After Anthropic's IPO Disappoints, Will OpenAI's Be Delayed Further? Kalshi Says 'Not Until the Second Half of Next Year' URL Source: http://en.fnnews.com/news/202611260239412071 Final URL: https://en.fnnews.com/news/202611260239412071 Published Time: 2026-11-26T03:05:34+09:00 Markdown Content: [Financial News] ![Image 1](https://image.fnnews.com/resource/media/image/2026/11/05/202611051908319770_l.jpg) Kalshi, a prediction market, forecast that an OpenAI IPO would be possible only in the second half of next year. The photo shows a cooling unit at an OpenAI data center in Abilene, Texas, on September 23 last year (local time). Reuters-Yonhap With rival Anthropic's IPO disappointing, expectations are growing that OpenAI's listing will also be delayed. According to CNBC on the 25th (local time), bettors on prediction market Kalshi put the odds of OpenAI launching an IPO by the end of the first half of next year at about 28%. The odds, which were above 50% until recently, plunged. The odds that OpenAI would go public by October next year were also put at 50-50. OpenAI was recently valued at $1.25 trillion (about 1.682 quadrillion won) in a fundraising round. OpenAI began its journey toward a public listing by filing a confidential IPO registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) last June, but is delaying its timeline as market conditions have turned unfavorable amid concerns about investment in AI. In an interview with Fortune last September, CEO Sam Altman ruled out plans to go public this year, citing concerns about AI safety. By contrast, rival Anthropic pushed ahead with the largest IPO in history on the 19th. It got off to a strong start. Demand was so strong that the company raised its offering price from $81 to $83, and its opening price on the first day of trading reached $111.50, 34.3% above the offering price. After climbing as high as $115.10 during the session, Anthropic ended its first day of trading at $97.17, up 17% from the offering price. However, as the market plunged amid a selloff in Nvidia, the stock subsequently turned lower. On the 24th, Anthropic fell below its $83 offering price. Its shares plunged nearly 30% from their peak. The market shifted from optimism about AI to concerns about AI. In particular, Democrats' landslide victory in the midterm elections on the 3rd is weighing on investor sentiment. Republican strongholds, including Texas, have flipped to Democrats, fueling concerns that AI data center construction in those areas will be disrupted. There is also a widespread expectation that discussions on AI regulation and congressional hearings will proliferate once a new federal Congress with a Democratic majority convenes in early January next year. dympna@fnnews.com Song Kyung-jae Reporter

records.title: Anthropic shares drop 28%, analysts warn of tougher OpenAI IPO
records.excerpt: Stock screener & analysis tools for Indian stock market. Click now to research, evaluate & filter stocks. Anthropic, PBC (NASDAQ: ANT) shares have fallen about 28% from their initial public offering high, signaling a cooling market for artificial intelligence listings. This decline prompts experts to warn that OpenAI may face a more challenging debut if it proceeds with its planned late-2027 listing. Tech analyst Luke Lango stated that the era of easy gains for AI companies has ended. "For OpenAI, the free pop is over," Lango said. He noted that public markets will now price OpenAI against Anthropic's current trading levels rather than its debut-day hype. ## Valuation pressures and market sentiment Anthropic priced its record IPO at $83 on November 19, raising $81.3 billion. The stock hit a high of $115.10 before dropping below the offer price this week. Lango described the current valuation as "pricey, not a meme valuation," noting the stock trades at roughly 40 times trailing sales and under 20 times its run rate. Jay Ritter, director of The IPO Initiative at the University of Florida, added that OpenAI "will have to lower its expectations" for its share price if Anthropic continues to underperform. Ritter emphasized that the first few days of trading are less critical than the subsequent two months. ## Chinese AI stocks as cautionary tale Recent listings in China provide a parallel example of rapid valuation unwinding. Z.AI Co. Ltd. and MiniMax Group Inc. both surged after their January Hong Kong debuts but have since fallen sharply from their peaks. | Company | Peak Decline | Current Status vs IPO Price | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Zhipu (Z.AI) | More than 90% below June high | About 106% above IPO price | | MiniMax Group | 93% below record high | About 47% below IPO price | Lango characterized these moves as "retail frenzies." He noted that Zhipu’s valuation, which briefly exceeded 1,000 times sales, lost its premium once lock-up periods expired. ## Historical context and future outlook Despite the negative short-term performance, historical data suggests volatility is common for high-profile tech listings. Facebook dropped by about 50% in the four months following its 2012 IPO before becoming an enormous success, Ritter noted. Overall, IPOs carry roughly a 50% chance of a negative return over three years. ## What the numbers show A divergence exists between Anthropic's operational fundamentals and its market reception. While the company raised $81.3 billion, indicating strong institutional demand at the offering stage, the 28% drop from the high suggests retail investors are repricing risk based on scarcity rather than long-term profitability. With Anthropic trading at 40 times trailing sales, the market appears to be shifting from valuing AI potential to demanding clearer paths to monetization, a hurdle OpenAI must clear if it lists in late 2027.

records.excerpt: Title: OpenAI asked investors to steer clear of xAI, Anthropic and three other named rivals URL Source: http://cryptobriefing.com/openai-asked-investors-avoid-funding-rivals/ Final URL: https://cryptobriefing.com/openai-asked-investors-avoid-funding-rivals/ Published Time: 2026-11-27T23:17:11+00:00 Markdown Content: During its $6.6 billion raise, OpenAI told backers it expected them to skip funding five competing AI startups [OpenAI](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/openai/) wanted investors’ money. It also wanted that money to stay away from its competitors. During its $6.6 billion funding round in October 2024, OpenAI asked participating investors not to back five rival firms: [Anthropic](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/anthropic/), Elon Musk’s xAI, Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence (SSI), and AI companies [Perplexity](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/perplexity/) and Glean. Frontier AI labs run on capital, so limiting a rival’s access to it, even informally, is a competitive tactic. ## What OpenAI actually asked for The October 2024 round valued OpenAI at between $150 billion and $157 billion. [Microsoft](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/microsoft/), [Nvidia](https://cryptobriefing.com/markets/nvidia/), SoftBank and Thrive Capital were among the backers. Along with the term sheet, OpenAI sent a clear message about loyalty: it asked backers to refrain from supporting the five named competitors. The request was not a formal legal requirement. OpenAI framed it as an expectation tied to meaningful involvement with the company. Investors were not contractually barred from writing checks elsewhere. They were simply put on notice about what OpenAI considered good-faith partnership. OpenAI had two goals. It wanted to limit rivals’ access to funding, and it wanted to keep sensitive information from flowing to competitors. Investors in a company like OpenAI can see strategy, product roadmaps and financial performance. An investor sitting at the table with OpenAI and Anthropic at the same time could, in theory, carry insights between the two. OpenAI’s request was meant to make that kind of overlap less likely. ## Competition kept going anyway Many venture firms kept stakes in both OpenAI and its competitors. OpenAI itself did not slow down. In March/April 2026, the company closed another funding round worth $122 billion at a post-money valuation of $852 billion. That’s up from the $150 billion to $157 billion range set in October 2024. Anthropic, one of the five names on OpenAI’s do-not-fund list, has also kept growing. The company has filed for a public offering that is expected in November 2026. If that listing proceeds, public market investors would get a direct way to back one of OpenAI’s most prominent competitors. ## Why exclusivity is hard to enforce in AI The way the request was structured explains much of its limited effect. A non-binding expectation carries social and relational weight, but it can’t be enforced in court. An investor who ignores it may risk a cooler relationship with OpenAI. They don’t face a lawsuit. There’s also the question of which rivals made the list. Anthropic and xAI are building frontier models. SSI, led by Sutskever, is focused on safe superintelligence. Perplexity and Glean are AI companies operating in other parts of the market. By naming all five, OpenAI showed it saw competitors beyond the companies building models. ## What this means for investors and AI labs The episode shows a tension between labs and investors that will likely persist. Leading AI companies want committed partners who won’t leak information or bankroll the competition. Investors want exposure to the whole sector, because nobody can say with certainty which lab will dominate. For AI labs, the lesson is that market leadership buys influence but not control. OpenAI’s scale is what let it make the request at all. Few startups could ask Microsoft, Nvidia and SoftBank to avoid other deals and expect to be taken seriously. Even so, capital still reached competitors. Anthropic’s expected November 2026 public offering is the next development to watch. A successful listing would give a direct OpenAI competitor access to money that private exclusivity requests can’t reach. The size of recent rounds also raises the stakes. When a single company can close a $122 billion round, competitors face pressure to raise comparable amounts. **Disclosure:** This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. records.title: Insuring SoftBank's Debt Costs the Most Since 2022 as OpenAI Doubts Grow
records.excerpt: SoftBank's 9.75% dollar bond from September has seen its risk premium jump about 40%, Bloomberg reported. Shareholders felt the strain too, with the stock OpenAI has no share price, so doubts about it are landing on the Japanese company that borrowed heavily to back it. You can read them in what lenders now charge, though an expensive warning is still a long way from a default. Protecting $10 million of SoftBank's debt against default now costs about $516,000 a year. Bloomberg reported that the company's five-year credit default swaps reached 516 basis points at 6:30 a.m. Tokyo time on Thursday, the highest since October 2022. A credit default swap works like insurance. You pay a yearly premium, the seller pays out if the borrower fails to pay its debts, and each basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point. A rising premium shows you how worried the market is. It doesn't show that SoftBank has missed a payment or is about to. S&P and Fitch both rated the company BB+, one step below investment grade, with a stable outlook as of November 10, SoftBank's investor briefing shows. Bondholders want more too. The spread on a 9.75% dollar bond SoftBank sold in September, meaning the extra yield investors demand over a safer benchmark, has widened about 40% to roughly 644 basis points, per Bloomberg. Investors are worried that returns on AI infrastructure could arrive too slowly to justify a buildout paid for with borrowed money, Reuters reported on Wednesday, and SoftBank sits right in the middle of that worry. Its shares dropped 14.83% that day to ¥2,696.50, Investing.com data show. Reuters put the November loss at almost 40%, leaving the stock on course for its worst month since 2000. SoftBank pushes for a full $10 billion loan against its OpenAI stake SoftBank has reopened talks with Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Mizuho for a $10 billion margin loan against its OpenAI stake, this time offering a personal repayment guarantee to win lenders over. The renewed push comes as OpenAI's IPO timeline slips toward 2027, the same year SoftBank must repay a separate $40 billion bridge loan tied to the same... - softbank 10 billion dollar loan openai - margin loan against private company stake Anthropic made things harder. The Claude developer closed at $81.91 on Tuesday, under its $83 offer price, in only its fourth day of trading, according to Bloomberg. When public buyers won't hold one leading AI lab at its offer price, you've got good reason to ask what they'd pay for OpenAI. Thursday brought shareholders some relief. SoftBank ended Tokyo's morning session up 11.3% at ¥3,000 as chip stocks bounced, MLQ reported, citing Yahoo Finance data. The swap reading was taken before that session opened, and half a day of buying doesn't repay any debt. A listed stand-in for OpenAI SoftBank's total investment in OpenAI reached $64.6 billion when the last $10 billion instalment went in on October 1, buying a stake of about 13%. On September 30, the company valued the $54.6 billion it had invested by then at $99.6 billion, and it booked no gain or loss on the holding over the previous six months because the valuation hadn't changed since March. A figure that stood still can't tell you how nervous anyone has become. SoftBank's shares, bonds and swaps get a new price every trading day, so they're the handiest place to act on doubts about OpenAI, even though Arm moves them too. The borrowing has been enormous. SoftBank raised $56.5 billion between July and September, a record quarter for the company. The haul included an $11.9 billion term loan, $11.1 billion of foreign bonds, a $10 billion loan linked to its OpenAI shares and a $5 billion increase that took its Arm margin loan facility to $25 billion. Much of the money went to clear a bridge loan, arranged at up to $40 billion, six months before its March 2027 due date. What happens if Arm or OpenAI loses value? Arm is the big cushion, and it's getting thinner. SoftBank's roughly 923 million Arm shares were worth $267 billion on September 30 and $172 billion on November 9, its slides show. At Tuesday's close of $161.56, our arithmetic gives about $149 billion. That's still close to six times the $25 billion facility, and the loan has no recourse to the parent company. SoftBank's slide on the deal doesn't say at what share price lenders could demand more collateral. The OpenAI loan ties SoftBank more directly to the private valuation. The company didn't pledge the shares, but the two-year loan agreed in August has a margin call trigger based on the OpenAI preferred stock held by its Vision Fund 2, and SoftBank guarantees the debt. A margin call is a lender's demand for extra security, usually cash. You won't find the trigger level in the briefing's summary of terms. For scale, every 10% cut to the September valuation of the stake would wipe about $10 billion off SoftBank's assets. Twenty-one banks just lined up behind SoftBank's $40 billion OpenAI bet SoftBank's $40 billion bridge loan for its OpenAI stake has expanded to include 21 new lenders, with First Abu Dhabi Bank, Singapore's GIC, and Standard Chartered each taking close to $1 billion. The loan's March 2027 maturity is the clearest signal yet that an OpenAI IPO is on the horizon. - SoftBank OpenAI $40 billion loan - SoftBank bridge financing OpenAI IPO SoftBank also has a limit of its own. It aims to keep net debt below 25% of the value of its holdings in normal times, with 35% as the upper threshold even in extraordinary ones. The ratio was 15.9% at the end of September. The company's November 9 update showed ¥56 trillion of holdings and ¥44.7 trillion left after net debt, which we calculate as a ratio of about 20%. That snapshot excluded the October payment to OpenAI and Arm's latest fall, and both would push the figure higher if nothing else moved. Cash gives the company some room. SoftBank reported a ¥5 trillion position at the end of September, about $32 billion, against ¥1.6 trillion of bond redemptions over two years, although the total counted an unused credit line and predated the October instalment. Its briefing says financial policy is unchanged, and lists turning assets into cash, asset-backed borrowing and a slower investment pace among the ways to manage the debt ratio. The same document shows a $5.4 billion purchase of ABB's robotics business still to come. records.title: OpenAI Asked Investors to Avoid Funding Five Competing AI Firms
records.excerpt: 2 min read Add as a preferred source on Google OpenAI Asked Investors to Avoid Funding Five Competing AI Firms The request accompanied OpenAI’s $6.6 billion October 2024 funding round and was not a formal legal restriction. By John Kim Published Nov 27, 2026, 6:21 PM EST Five sealed glass doors surround a brightly lit central atrium / TokenPost.ai OpenAI asked investors in its October 2024 funding round to avoid backing five competing artificial intelligence companies, seeking to limit rival financing and reduce the risk of information flowing between competitors. The companies named were Anthropic, Elon Musk’s xAI, Ilya Sutskever’s Safe Superintelligence (SSI), Perplexity and Glean. OpenAI’s request accompanied a $6.6 billion funding round that valued the company at between $150 billion and $157 billion. Microsoft, Nvidia, SoftBank and Thrive Capital were among the investors in the round. OpenAI presented the request as an expectation tied to meaningful involvement with the company, rather than as a contractual restriction. Investors were not legally barred from funding the named rivals. But investors in OpenAI can gain access to its strategy, product roadmaps and financial performance, creating a risk that sensitive information could move between competing businesses. The nonbinding request did not prevent some investors from backing competitors. OpenAI later closed a $122 billion funding round in March or April 2026 at an $852 billion post-money valuation. Anthropic, one of the companies named in OpenAI’s request, has filed for a public offering expected in November 2026. If the listing proceeds, public-market investors would have a direct way to invest in one of OpenAI’s major competitors. The episode highlights a conflict between AI companies seeking committed financial partners and investors seeking exposure across the sector. OpenAI’s scale allowed it to ask backers to avoid rival investments, but the request did not stop capital from reaching competing companies. records.title: AI Cost Pressure Deepens as Anthropic and OpenAI Post Heavy Losses
records.excerpt: Anthropic posted a $104 billion loss through the first three quarters of 2026, while OpenAI recorded a $10.9 billion adjusted operating loss in the third quarter. 2 min read Add as a preferred source on Google AI Cost Pressure Deepens as Anthropic and OpenAI Post Heavy Losses Anthropic posted a $104 billion loss through the first three quarters of 2026, while OpenAI recorded a $10.9 billion adjusted operating loss in the third quarter. By John Kim Published Nov 26, 2026, 9:14 AM EST Industrial cooling towers beside a massive data center at dusk / TokenPost.ai Anthropic and OpenAI are posting substantial revenue while absorbing heavy losses, highlighting the financial pressure created by high computing costs and cheaper artificial intelligence alternatives. Anthropic posted a net loss of $104 billion through the first three quarters of 2026 on revenue of $33.2 billion. About $94.3 billion of the loss came from noncash adjustments tied to financing instruments. OpenAI generated about $10 billion in revenue during the third quarter of 2026, a 50% increase from the previous quarter. Its adjusted operating loss reached $10.9 billion for the quarter. The figures have increased investor scrutiny of AI valuations. Anthropic was valued at approximately $1.5 trillion after its initial public offering in mid-November 2026, but Anthropic’s shares declined shortly after opening. TokenPost previously examined Anthropic’s IPO valuation . The companies also face a difficult pricing environment. Leading U.S. models charge between $2 and $40 per million tokens, while cheaper open-source models and Chinese AI labs offer alternatives at substantially lower costs. Anthropic has committed more than $900 billion in leases and purchases extending through 2045. Those obligations tie the company to long-term infrastructure spending as it seeks to maintain demand for premium AI services. Arthur Hayes, the former BitMEX executive, has forecast that closed-source AI companies may eventually become government contractors. His view rests partly on the availability of lower-cost open-source models and businesses’ reluctance to share proprietary data with outside AI providers, which can limit enterprise commitment. Neither company has said it plans to make government contracting a central part of its business. The companies’ financial results and infrastructure commitments will remain central to scrutiny of their valuations as the AI market develops. 英中銀の報告書が示唆するのは、時計がもう1つあるかもしれないという可能性だ。AIが古典的なコンピューターの上で動く新しい解読法を見つければ、量子コンピューターの完成時期とは無関係に期限が来る。しかも、その時計の針がどこまで進んでいるのかは、AI企業が公開している情報だけでは分からない。 だとすれば、移行計画の「いつまでに」を議論する前に確かめておくことがある。自社のシステムのどこで、どの暗号が、何を守るために使われているのかを、委託先も含めて一覧にできているか。暗号方式を短期間で差し替えられる設計（クリプトアジリティ）になっているか。移行先のPQCもまた、現時点では効率的に解けないと考えられている数学の問題に依拠しているからだ。 クリプトアジリティの重要性は、金融庁の2024年の報告書がすでに指摘していた。英中銀の金融安定報告書も、PQCへの移行を終えた後であっても、新しい暗号技術に適応する能力が不足すれば脆弱性が再び生じうると明記している。日英の当局が同じ結論に達しているわけだ。 英国の金融当局は、数学界の知らせが届く前から、AIと暗号を自分たちの問題として扱っていた。問われているのは、暗号がいつ破られるかを言い当てることではない。いつ破られても対応できる組織になっているかどうかだ。あなたの組織では、リスクの棚卸しはどこまで進んでいるだろうか。 小林 啓倫（こばやし・あきひと） 経営コンサルタント。1973年東京都生まれ。獨協大学卒、筑波大学大学院修士課程修了。 システムエンジニアとしてキャリアを積んだ後、米バブソン大学にてMBAを取得。その後コンサルティングファーム、国内ベンチャー企業、大手メーカー等で先端テクノロジーを活用した事業開発に取り組む。エンジニアとしての実務経験を土台に、AIやセキュリティ事情にも精通しており、テクノロジーと地政学・経済安全保障の交差領域まで、幅広い分野の動向を追う。著書に『 FinTechが変える! records.label: finance.biggo.jp
records.title: OpenAIの最新モデル、200年前の匿名スケッチブック作者を22分で特定 歴史研究に一石
records.excerpt: カナダ・ウィルフリッド・ローリエ大学のマーク・ハンフリーズ教授が、OpenAIのGPT-6.2 Astraを使い、1808年制作の匿名スケッチブックの作者を22分で特定した。イェール大学バイネッケ稀覯書・手稿図書館所蔵の資料で、作者はフランス貴族のシャボー子爵と判明。モデルは毛皮商人の日記など一次資料を横断照合して候補を絞り、日記の筆跡・日付・構図がスケッチと一致した。OpenAIのブロックマン社長は称賛したが、ハンフリーズ氏は技術の限界も強調し、歴史学への影響は数学ほど深刻ではないとの見方を示した。 OpenAIが投入した最新のAIモデル「GPT-6.2 Astra」が、専門の歴史学者でも特定できなかった1808年制作の匿名スケッチブックの作者をわずか22分で突き止めた。カナダ・ウィルフリッド・ローリエ大学で歴史学教授を務めるマーク・ハンフリーズ（Mark Humphries）氏が2026年11月下旬に明らかにしたもので、AIによる推論が数学のような決定論的な領域を超え、歴史学のような非決定論的な分野にも応用可能であることを示す事例として注目を集めている。 問題となったのは、米イェール大学のバイネッケ稀覯書・手稿図書館が所蔵する旅行スケッチブックだ。1808年にカナダのモントリオールとフォート・ウィリアムを往復した旅を描いたもので、同館が2020年に古書店から購入するまで存在自体が知られていなかった。まだら模様の革表紙で全84ページのうち34ページに鉛筆とインクによるデッサンや水彩画が収められており、要塞や家屋などの建築物、船から望む海岸線、馬に引かせるそり、現地の人々の姿などが描かれている。短いキャプションはあるものの、日付が記されているのは3ページのみだった。 作者特定が困難を極めた背景には、記録されたルートのありふれた性質がある。当時、年間数百隻の船が同じ航路を行き交っており、作者候補は数千人規模に上る可能性があった。加えて当時の資料はほぼすべてが手書きで索引も整備されておらず、検索作業の効率は極めて低い。ハンフリーズ氏自身も長年調査を続けながら、決め手となる手がかりを得られずにいた。 ハンフリーズ氏は2026年10月下旬、かねて注目していたAIと歴史学の接点を探るためGPT-6.2 Astraのテストを開始。18世紀の商人が記した数千行に及ぶ帳簿をCSV形式に転写し検証させるなど、その能力を確認していた。その上で、あえて不可能と思われる課題として、スケッチブックの画像へのアクセス権と若干の背景情報を与え、作者の特定を指示した。 モデルが導き出した答えは、フランスの小貴族ルイ＝ギー＝シャルル＝ギヨーム・ド・ロアン＝シャボー子爵（Louis-Guy-Charles-Guillaume de Rohan-Chabot）だった。さらに、クリーブランド州立大学の特別コレクションが所蔵するアーカイブ目録から同子爵の旅行記の複製を取り寄せ、仮説を検証するよう促した。ハンフリーズ氏は当初、シャボー子爵なる人物に心当たりがなかったが、調査を進めると実在が確認できる。同子爵は亡命先の英国で陸軍将校となり、1808年の大半をカナダで過ごしていた。北米やカナダの歴史家の間でもほとんど知られておらず、2019年に刊行された毛皮商人ジョージ・ネルソンの日記に、フォート・ウィリアムを訪れたとの記述が残る程度だった。 半信半疑のまま日記を取り寄せたハンフリーズ氏は、筆跡がスケッチブックの特徴的な文字と一致すること、滞在時期が重なることを確認する。決め手となったのは1808年6月18日、セント・ジョセフ砦に到着した後に同砦のスケッチを描いたとする記述で、構図がスケッチブックの一枚と符合した。日記には162ページにわたり毛皮貿易会社の文書や日誌、手紙の抜粋が記されており、当時の毛皮貿易研究にとって貴重な一次資料になると同氏は指摘する。 GPT-6.2 Astraの推論過程を追跡したところ、スケッチブックの各ページを順に確認した上で、歴史家が用いるのと同じアーカイブサイトから入手可能な一次資料を網羅的に照合し、毛皮商人ジョセフ・フロビシャーの日記にシャボー子爵への言及を見つけて足取りをたどったことが判明した。ハンフリーズ氏は、事後に経路を検証することは可能でも、人間の歴史家が同じ道筋で作者に到達するのは極めて難しいとの見方を示している。 項目 内容 使用モデル GPT-6.2 Astra（OpenAI） 特定までの時間 22分 対象資料 1808年制作の旅行スケッチブック（全84ページ、うち34ページに素描） 所蔵 イェール大学バイネッケ稀覯書・手稿図書館 特定された作者 ルイ＝ギー＝シャルル＝ギヨーム・ド・ロアン＝シャボー子爵 検証資料 シャボー子爵の日記（筆跡・日付・構図が一致） 注：ハンフリーズ氏の公表内容および報道に基づき作成 AI業界の反応は迅速だった。OpenAIのグレッグ・ブロックマン（Greg Brockman）社長はハンフリーズ氏の投稿をリポストし、モデルが「重大な歴史的謎」を解いたと称賛。技術者らもSNS上で驚きや祝意を相次いで寄せた。一方、歴史学界の受け止めは比較的冷静で、人間にも同様の調査は可能だとの指摘も出ている。ハンフリーズ氏自身、スケッチブックの作者特定が数学のリーマン予想を解くのと同列の意義を持つとは考えていない。 同氏はテクノロジーに対する姿勢について「世間が思うよりはるかに両義的だ」と述べ、自らは執筆にAIを使わないと明かす。その上で「この技術には現実的な限界がある。モデルがなし得ることを示したかった」と語り、歴史家がAIの得意分野と限界を正確に把握すべきだとの考えを示した。歴史学は単一の普遍的な真理を追うのではなく、変化する現在に照らして過去を解釈し直す学問であり、ある種の人間性が不可欠だとして、AIの影響は数学ほど深刻にはならないとの見方を示している。 市場への直接的な影響は限定的だが、生成AIの用途がコード生成や文章作成から、一次資料の横断照合を伴う専門調査へと広がりつつあることを示す材料となる。AIエージェントによる調査支援は、学術・法務・金融リサーチなど文書照合を業務の中核に据える分野での需要拡大が想定される。ハンフリーズ氏は2027年春から夏にかけ、人間には不可能な成果を上げるAIエージェントへの対応に歴史家が苦慮し、自信を揺らす可能性があると予測する一方、学問としての歴史学の土台は揺るがないとの立場を崩していない。
records.evidence: Google News RSSで「OpenAIの最新モデル、200年前の匿名スケッチブック作者を22分で特定 歴史研究に一石」を確認し、配信元ページhttps://finance.biggo.jp/news/c0796cbc-5ad3-49c7-bb40-db53747be154を特定した。本文抽出: カナダ・ウィルフリッド・ローリエ大学のマーク・ハンフリーズ教授が、OpenAIのGPT-6.2 Astraを使い、1808年制作の匿名スケッチブックの作者を22分で特定した。イェール大学バイネッケ稀覯書・手稿図書館所蔵の資料で、作者はフランス貴族のシャボー子爵と判明。モデルは毛皮商人の日記など一次資料を横断照合して候補を絞り、日記の筆跡・日付・構図がスケッチと一致した。OpenAIのブロックマン社長は称賛したが、ハンフリーズ氏は技術の限界も強調し、歴史学への影響は数学ほど深刻ではないとの見方を示した。 OpenAIが投入した最新のAIモデル「GPT-6.2 Astra」が、専門の歴史学者でも特定できなかった1808年制作の匿名スケッチブックの作者をわずか22分で突き止めた。カナダ・ウィルフリッド・ローリエ大学で歴史学教授を務めるマーク・ハンフリーズ（Mark Humphries）氏が2026年11月下旬に明らかにしたもので、AIによる推論が数学のような決定論的な領域を超え、歴史学のような非決定論的な分野にも応用可能であることを示す事例として注目を集めている。 問題となったのは、米イェール大学のバイネッケ稀覯書・手稿図書館が所蔵する旅行スケッチブックだ。1808年にカナダのモントリオールとフォート・ウィリアムを往復した旅を描いたもので、同館が2020年に古書店から購入するまで存在自体が知られていなかった。まだら模様の革表紙で全84ページのうち34ページに鉛筆とインクによるデッサンや水彩画が収められており、要塞や家屋などの建築物、船から望む海岸線、馬に引かせるそり、現地の人々の姿な

records.excerpt: Title: Mathematicians Slam Anthropic Researcher’s Proof Joke as Saudi Engineer in OpenAI Bugging Case Faces $1M Bond URL Source: http://www.tekedia.com/mathematicians-slam-anthropic-researchers-proof-joke-as-saudi-engineer-in-openai-bugging-case-faces-1m-bond/ Final URL: https://www.tekedia.com/mathematicians-slam-anthropic-researchers-proof-joke-as-saudi-engineer-in-openai-bugging-case-faces-1m-bond/ Published Time: 2026-11-26T14:58:30+00:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Mathematicians Slam Anthropic Researcher’s Proof Joke as Saudi Engineer in OpenAI Bugging Case Faces $1M Bond](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/mathematics-768x432.png) Mathematicians are pushing back against an Anthropic researcher’s joke about a 250,000-page mathematical proof, while a Saudi engineer accused of using OpenAI’s vibe-coding technology to bug his office is reportedly set to be released on a $1 million bond. The stories highlight the growing intersection of artificial intelligence, scientific debate, workplace security and the legal risks surrounding rapidly evolving technology. The controversy among mathematicians began after an Anthropic researcher made a joke referencing an extraordinarily lengthy proof reportedly spanning 250,000 pages. Although the remark may have been intended as humor about the growing complexity of mathematical research and artificial intelligence, it quickly drew criticism from members of the mathematical community. Researchers have increasingly been sensitive to how AI companies portray mathematics, particularly when claims or jokes could blur the distinction between genuine scientific breakthroughs and speculative technological narratives. Mathematics has historically relied on rigorous verification, peer review and reproducibility. A proof, regardless of its length, must demonstrate that a conclusion logically follows from established assumptions. [![Image 2](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/invest-masterclass.jpg)](https://school.tekedia.com/course/masterclass/) The idea of a 250,000-page proof has therefore become a provocative subject, raising questions about whether mathematical knowledge could become increasingly difficult for humans to independently verify as AI systems generate increasingly complex arguments. Critics argue that jokes involving enormous proofs risk trivializing the intellectual discipline and reinforcing misconceptions about mathematical research. Others may see the controversy as evidence of the growing tension between traditional academic culture and the increasingly influential technology companies developing AI tools. [![Image 3](https://www.tekedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/parrot-2.jpg)](https://capital.tekedia.com/course/fee/) As AI systems become capable of assisting with advanced reasoning, mathematicians are confronting new questions about authorship, verification and the limits of machine-generated knowledge. Meanwhile, a separate legal controversy involving a Saudi engineer accused of bugging an OpenAI office has drawn attention to the potential misuse of AI-powered software in workplace environments. The engineer is reportedly set to be released on a $1 million bond, following allegations that he used OpenAI’s vibe-coding application to facilitate the installation or operation of surveillance equipment. Vibe-coding tools allow users to create software by describing what they want in ordinary language rather than manually writing extensive code. These applications have become increasingly popular because they lower the barriers to software development, enabling individuals with limited programming experience to build applications, automate tasks and experiment with technical projects. The same accessibility that makes vibe-coding attractive raises concerns about misuse. Investigators in cases involving alleged surveillance. Unauthorized access or malicious software must determine whether technological tools were deliberately exploited and whether the accused individual violated applicable laws. The allegations involving the Saudi engineer underscore how AI-assisted development can intersect with criminal investigations and corporate security concerns. Yet allegations remain allegations, and the legal process must establish responsibility through evidence rather than assumptions about the technology involved. The stories illustrate the complicated relationship between artificial intelligence and institutions that depend on trust, accountability and rigorous standards. In mathematics, AI challenges established expectations about how knowledge is produced and verified. In corporate environments, AI-assisted programming introduces new capabilities that can potentially be misused. As AI continues to evolve, the debate will extend beyond technological innovation to questions about responsibility, security, intellectual integrity and oversight. The challenge will be ensuring that increasingly powerful tools strengthen scientific progress and productivity without undermining the institutions and safeguards that make those advances meaningful.

records.title: OpenAIがプライバシー推論で企業顧客を獲得、GPT-6.2の課金誤り修正が逆にユーザーの利用枠消費を4割加速
records.excerpt: OpenAIの最高経営責任者（CEO）サム・アルトマン氏はプライバシー推論モードを発表した。ゼロデータ保持（ZDR）機構を伴い、データは処理後に即座に消去され、OpenAI内部の人員は元の内容に触れることができない。金融や医療などデータ漏洩に極めて敏感な大企業顧客を狙う。一方、技術責任者のティボ・ソティオー氏はGPT-6.2公開期間中に利用量の課金誤りがあったことを認めた。修正後、ユーザーが同じ作業をAstraで行うと利用枠の上限に達する速度が40%速まり、Solでは25%速まった。OpenAIは過去の差額を追徴せず、有料ユーザーに一度の利用枠リセットを提供すると約束した。開発者コミュニティは、利用枠の厳格化とモデルの推論トークン減少が同時に起きたことを批判し、企業向けに資源を傾けていると見ている。 OpenAIは計算資源と商業の重心を同時に企業向けへ傾けつつある。同社CEOのサム・アルトマン（Sam Altman）氏は「プライバシー推論モード」を対外発表し、企業顧客がOpenAIに基盤データを開示することなく最先端モデルを呼び出せるようにした。ほぼ同時期に、OpenAIの技術責任者ティボ・ソティオー（Tibo Sottiaux）氏はX上で、GPT-6.2の公開期間中に利用量の課金誤りがあったことを認め、修正後はユーザーが利用枠の上限に達する速度が明らかに速まると述べた。二つの動きが重なり、開発者コミュニティで強い反発を引き起こしている。 『36Kr』の報道によると、今回導入されたプライバシー推論モードにはゼロデータ保持（ZDR）機構が付随し、データは処理完了後すぐに消去され、OpenAI内部のセキュリティ審査プロセスは元の内容に触れることなく自動で実行できる。この設計が狙うのは、大企業が長年抱えてきた懸念そのものである。中核コードや財務データがひとたびモデルに入れば、次世代モデルの訓練に使われるのではないか——という懸念だ。OpenAIにとってこれは、収益構造が個人のサブスクリプション料から年間数百万ドル、さらには数千万ドル規模の企業向けカスタム契約へ移ることを意味する。 企業向けの「金庫」と対照的なのが、一般の有料ユーザーが直面する利用枠の厳格化だ。ソティオー氏は現地時間11月25日、X上で、GPT-6.2の提供開始時にシステムが大多数のユーザーのAstraとSolの利用量を十分に差し引いていなかったと説明した。これは課金の誤りであり、現在は修正済みだという。修正の直接的な結果として、同じ作業を完了する際にユーザーがGPT-6.2 Astraで流量上限に達する速度は先週より40%速まり、Solでは25%速まった。 項目 修正前 修正後 GPT-6.2 Astraの利用枠上限到達速度 基準 40%加速 GPT-6.2 Solの利用枠上限到達速度 基準 25%加速 過去の差額費用 不足分の差し引き 追徴せず 補償措置 — 有料ユーザーに一度の利用枠リセット 注：データはOpenAI公式説明によるもので、比較基準は先週の水準。 ソティオー氏は同時に二点の安心材料を示した。これまで少なく差し引いていた利用量についてユーザーに追加請求は行わない。誤りによる不便への補償として、すべての有料プランのユーザーに一度の利用枠リセットの機会を提供する。同氏は前日にも、ChatGPT Businessチームも同様に一度のリセット枠を取得し、高速応答モードを12月31日まで無料開放すると述べていた。同氏は、修正後であってもAstraとSolの単位利用量あたりの生産性は前世代のGPT-6 AstraとGPT-6.1 Solを依然として上回っており、他のモデルは今回の誤りの影響を受けていないと強調した。 AstraとSolは11月17日に公開された。前者は文書、スライド、プログラミングなどの高品質な専門業務に位置づけられ、後者は日常的なオフィス業務を担い、ChatGPT WorkとCodexのPlus、Pro、Enterprise、Eduユーザーをカバーする。AIモデル評価機関Artificial Analysisのデータによると、Solの単一タスクあたりのコストはGPT-6 Astraの約15%で、Astraは総合知能指数でClaude Fable 5.2に次いで2位となっている。別の報道によれば、OpenAIは11月25日から一部のProユーザーについてChatとWorkの利用量枠を統合した。 開発者コミュニティの不満は「知能の低下」と「値上げ」が同時に起きている点に集中している。一部のテスト報告では、Astra 6.2とSol 6.2のいずれも出力トークンと推論トークンが明らかに減少しており、推論トークンの低下は統計的に有意で、モデルが深い思考に充てる計算資源が圧縮されたことを意味する。一部のユーザーから見れば、利用枠の消費加速とモデルの思考の浅薄化は同じことを指している。OpenAIはより低コストで同じリクエストを処理しつつある、というわけだ。 商業的な論理から見れば、この取捨選択は理解しにくいものではない。最先端モデルの単回の訓練と推論のコストは高く、C向けのサブスクリプション料では計算資源の支出を賄いきれない。支払い能力のより高い企業顧客へ資源を傾けることは、OpenAIの収益構造における能動的な調整である。問題は実行の仕方にある。課金誤りの修正自体は合理的だが、ユーザーが感じ取るのは利用可能枠の縮小とモデル性能の低下が同時に訪れることであり、公式のコミュニケーションは技術的な説明の域にとどまっている。 競争環境がこうした不満の出口を提供している。AnthropicのClaudeはコードと長文処理で優位を保ち、GoogleのGeminiは自社エコシステムに依拠し、中国国内のモデルは価格と反復速度で圧力をかけ続けている。企業顧客にとって、プライバシー推論とゼロデータ保持は調達判断における必須の要件であり、OpenAIの今回の動きは金融、医療、大型製造業の市場を開く可能性がある。一方、個人開発者や中小チームにとっては、移行コストが再計算されつつある。 注目すべきは、プライバシー推論モードが依存する計算資源がどこから来るのかという点だ。企業向けカスタムサービスが大量の推論資源を独占する必要があれば、C向け製品の利用枠政策とモデル仕様は引き続き圧迫される可能性がある。OpenAIはプライバシー推論の価格と提供開始のスケジュールをまだ公表しておらず、企業収益への貢献も今後の決算で検証する必要がある。

records.title: 生成AIのOpenAI、ChatGPTなどでGPT-5.6の一部モデルを提供終了へ
records.excerpt: 生成AIのOpenAI、ChatGPTなどでGPT-5.6の一部モデルを提供終了へ Home News 生成AIのOpenAI、ChatGPTなどでGPT-5.6の一部モデルを提供終了へ 2026/11/27 Startup Portfolio 生成AIのOpenAI、ChatGPTなどでGPT-5.6の一部モデルを提供終了へ OpenAIは、通常のChatGPTで選択できるGPT-5.6 Solと、ChatGPT WorkおよびCodexで利用できるGPT-5.6 SolとTerraの提供を終了すると告知しました。対象は製品ごとに異なり、通常のChatGPTでの告知対象はSolです。利用者が旧モデルを手動で選んでいる場合も、今後は終了後は別のモデルを選ぶ必要があります。 これに先立ち、同社は通常のChatGPTの「Chat」タブで、対話向けに調整したGPT-6.2 Solの段階的な提供を始めました。対象はPlus、Pro、Business、Enterpriseで、Enterpriseでは管理者の設定によって利用可否が異なります。同社の社内評価では、特に難しい指示への追従率がGPT-6の62.5%からGPT-6.2の78.1%に上がりました。この数字は通常のChatGPT向けの評価で、WorkやCodexで同じ改善幅を示したものではありません。 GPT-6.2 AstraとSolは、WorkとCodexでも別途プレビュー提供されています。業務でモデルを固定している場合は、文章の形式やツールの使い方など、既存のプロンプトが移行先でも期待どおりに動くかを個別に確かめると判断しやすくなります。今回の告知で示されたのはChatGPT、Work、Codexの提供変更であり、同名のAPIモデルの終了までを知らせるものではありません。 OpenAIについて OpenAIとは、2015年に設立された米国サンフランシスコのAI研究開発企業です。対話型AIのChatGPTに加え、ソフトウェア開発を支援するCodexを提供しています。開発者向けのAPIでは、企業がモデルを自社の製品や業務システムに組み込めます。GPTシリーズは文章や画像などを扱い、製品によって社内資料の調査やコードの作成にも利用できます。研究したモデルを一般利用者向けと開発者向けの双方に展開している点が特徴です。 Tags AI United States 関連ニュース 生成AIのOpenAI、ChatGPTのChatとWorkをまとめた画面を一部のPro利用者で試験 2026/11/28 AI会計ERPのDualEntry、在庫管理と原価計算を総勘定元帳に統合 2026/11/28 AIソフトウェア開発のCognition、CEOがAI普及に伴う情報漏えいリスクを指摘 2026/11/28 生成AIのAnthropic、AIエージェントが隔離環境の制約を外れる行動を測るSirenを公開 2026/11/28 細胞AIのCellular Intelligence、測定ノイズとモデル性能の関係を示す共同研究を公表 2026/11/28 音声AIのSarvam AI、英語とインドの22言語に対応する音声入力APIを公開 2026/11/28 検索AIのPerplexity、過去時点のウェブを検索できるTime Machineを公開 2026/11/27 フリート決済のCoast、ユタ州の拠点を50人に拡大し現場事業者向けの支援体制を強化 2026/11/27 Source Link OpenAI に興味がありますか？ 彼らの技術を貴社の事業に活かすため、我々がサポートできることがあるかもしれません。ウェブ会議で少し話をしませんか？(営業目的でのお問い合わせはお断りしております。) 最新ニュース 音声AIのSarvam AI、英語とインドの22言語に対応する音声入力APIを公開 2026/11/28 細胞AIのCellular Intelligence、測定ノイズとモデル性能の関係を示す共同研究を公表 2026/11/28 生成AIのAnthropic、AIエージェントが隔離環境の制約を外れる行動を測るSirenを公開 2026/11/28 AIソフトウェア開発のCognition、CEOがAI普及に伴う情報漏えいリスクを指摘 2026/11/28 AI会計ERPのDualEntry、在庫管理と原価計算を総勘定元帳に統合 2026/11/28 Contact AT PARTNERSにご相談ください お問い合わせフォーム

弘暉、以下「Fhill」）は、求職者が就職・転職の相談をしたときにAIが紹介する企業を業界別に順位づけした「AI推薦企業ランキング」を公開しました。24業界を対象に、ChatGPTの回答に企業名が挙がる割合（言及率）を毎月計測・更新します。企業は自社と競合の順位、言及率、AIからの語られ方を無料で確認できます。 ▼AI推薦企業ランキングサイトはこちら https://www.fhill.co.jp/lp/aio-geo/visibility-index [画像: https://prcdn.freetls.fastly.net/release_image/190074/2/190074-2-7a58596cfb886dfd29314e3798560539-1200x630.png?width=536&quality=85%2C75&format=jpeg&auto=webp&fit=bounds&bg-color=fff ] ■ 背景：求職者の企業探しは「AIへの相談」へ 生成AIの普及により、求職者の企業探しは「検索して比べる」から「AIに相談して絞り込む」へと移りつつあります。生成AIを利用したことがある2027年卒学生のうち75.8%が就職活動でも生成AIを活用しており（※1）、中途採用でも、求職活動で生成AIを活用した経験がある求職者は41.8%にのぼります（※2）。 求職者がAIに「介護の仕事でおすすめの会社は？」と尋ねたとき、回答に挙がるのは数社です。そこに名前がない企業は、求人を出していても比較の候補に入りません。一方で、自社がAIの回答にどのくらい登場しているのか、競合と比べてどの位置にいるのかを確かめる手段は、これまでほとんどありませんでした。 「採用AIO（Recruiting AI Optimization）」とは、求職者がChatGPTなどのAIに企業のことを聞いたとき、自社が候補に挙がり、正しく説明・推奨されるように採用サイトと外部の情報を整える取り組みです。Fhillは採用AIOの支援を通じて、多くの企業のAIでの見え方を診断してきました（採用AIOの詳しい解説： https://www.fhill.co.jp/blog/recruiting-aio-introduction ）。その知見をもとに、業界ごとの状況を誰でも確認できる指標として整備したのが「AI推薦企業ランキング」です。 ※1 株式会社i-plug「27卒学生と企業を対象としたChatGPT等の活用に関する調査」（2026年2月9日発表、27卒学生の有効回答512件） https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000200.000041771.html ※2 株式会社アイデム「2025年12月イーアイデム会員対象 仕事探しに関するアンケート調査」（2026年2月発表） https://www.aidem.co.jp/company/topics/data/20260203/index.html ■「AI推薦企業ランキング」の概要 AI推薦企業ランキングは、求職者がChatGPTに「どの会社で働くべきか」を相談したとき、AIがどの企業の名前を挙げるかを業界ごとに毎月計測し、言及率の高い順に並べたものです。企業は、同じ業界で採用を競う他社と自社の位置を比べられます。特徴は次のとおりです。 1. 24業界を、職種単位で計測 「ソフトウェアエンジニア」「コンサルタント」「看護師」「施工管理」「MR（医薬情報担当者）」「タクシー乗務員」など、専門職・営業職・現場職まで、業界ごとに求職者が多い職種を設定し、その職種の仕事探しでAIが候補に挙げる企業を比較します。 2. 求職者が本当に気にする10テーマで質問 総合的なおすすめ、給与・年収、定着・離職率、成長・キャリア、社風・人間関係、福利厚生、残業・働き方、安定性・将来性、応募・選考のしやすさ、女性活躍・多様性の10テーマで質問を設計。企業ごとに、どのテーマの相談で名前が挙がりやすいかがわかります。 3. 毎月同じ質問で計測し直す 毎月同じ質問で計測するため、変化を追えます。 ※掲載企業は本調査の測定対象です。掲載自体は、各社による本サービスの利用・協賛・推奨を示すものではありません。 ■調査結果の例：製造・工場業界 / IT・ソフトウェア業界 製造・工場業界（対象職種：製造オペレーター・期間工、掲載179社）では、デンソーが言及率51.7%で1位となり、SUBARU（同40.0%）、トヨタ自動車（同40.0%）が続きました。言及率が10%以上だったのは19社でした。 [表1: https://prtimes.jp/data/corp/190074/table/2_1_d51160422107258a75ce638407a89f7e.jpg?v=202611281645 ] ※上記は、2026年11月3日時点の調査結果です。 IT・ソフトウェア業界（対象職種：ソフトウェアエンジニア、掲載163社）では、NTTデータが言及率46.7%で1位となり、SCSK（同43.3%）、メルカリ（同41.7%）が続きました。 [表2: https://prtimes.jp/data/corp/190074/table/2_2_d86312f76e2e32d73a2b71656675b50b.jpg?v=202611281645 ] ※上記は、2026年11月3日時点の調査結果です。 ■業界別の1位 全24業界の1位企業と言及率は次のとおりです。1位企業の言及率は18.3%から91.7%まで業界によって大きく異なりました。1位でも言及率が40%に満たない業界では、AIが薦める企業がまだ定まっておらず、情報の発信次第で、これまで名前が挙がっていなかった企業がAIに推薦される余地があります。 [表3: https://prtimes.jp/data/corp/190074/table/2_3_49dc6737a03d3cfcb4c0fb4b678a47f5.jpg?v=202611281645 ] ※上記は、2026年11月3日時点の調査結果です。 ■ランキングの仕組み - 求職者の質問を固定する： 求職者がAIに実際に投げている「どの会社がいいか」の質問をもとに、業界ごとに共通の質問を設計し、毎月同じ質問で計測します。 - 10のテーマで質問する：給与・年収、残業・働き方、定着・離職率など、求職者が重視する10のテーマごとに質問を用意します。企業ごとに、どのテーマの相談で名前が挙がりやすいかが分かります。 - Web検索ありのChatGPTに聞く：求職者の利用が多いChatGPTに、Web検索を有効にした状態で質問し、回答をそのまま記録します。（※ランキングはChatGPTの回答をもとにしており、Gemini・Google AI Overview・Google AI Modeでの見え方は「採用AIO診断」で個社ごとに確認できます。） - 言及率を出す：業界ごとに、全回答のうち各企業の名前が登場した回答の割合（言及率）を出し、高い順に並べます。 - 毎月更新する：同じ質問で毎月計測し直し、順位と言及率を更新します。 ■企業ページでわかること 掲載企業ごとに専用ページがあり、次の内容を無料で確認できます。 ・言及率と業界内の順位 ・名前が挙がりやすい相談テーマ ・AIの回答からの抜粋（好意的に語られた点。掲載がある企業のみ） AIが自社のサイトを根拠に答えているか（引用率）、競合との比較、何から直すかの優先順位は、「採用AIO診断」（無料）でレポートします。詳しくは後述の「『採用AIO診断レポート』のご案内」をご覧ください。 ■調査概要 [表4: records.title: 住友生命がChatGPT Enterprise導入で推定ROI 203%を達成｜使い込むほど効果が上がる仕組みと久留米・福岡中小企業への活用ヒント
records.excerpt: OpenAIは2026年11月18日、日本の大手生命保険会社・住友生命のChatGPT Enterprise活用事例を公式サイトに掲載しました。全社推定ROI 203%、ヘビーユーザー（月101回以上）では推定524%という数値が注目を集めています。これらは従業員の時間短縮の自己申告を基にした推計値ですが、日本の大手企業でAI投資対効果が具体的な数字として示された点は、中小企業のAI導入判断にも示唆を与えます。 OpenAIは 2026年11月18日 、日本の大手生命保険会社・住友生命の ChatGPT Enterprise活用事例を公式カスタマーストーリーとして公開しました （出典：openai.com）。 全社の推定ROIは 203% 、月101回以上使用するヘビーユーザー層では推定 524% という数値が示されており、 国内での生成AI活用事例として注目を集めています。 何が起きたか 住友生命は2025年にChatGPT Businessで約100〜150名の社内パイロットを実施し、 2026年6月にChatGPT Enterpriseへ移行 して数千人規模に展開しました。 週次利用率は発行アカウントの80%超と報告されています。 利用頻度別の推定ROIは以下の通りです （従業員の自己申告による時間短縮を基にした推計値で、監査済み財務数値ではありません）。 月8〜15回利用： 推定ROI 55% 月16〜30回利用： 推定ROI 231% 月101回以上（ヘビーユーザー）： 推定ROI 524% 全社平均： 推定ROI 203% 住友生命は金融機関として自社のセキュリティ基準に照らしてEnterprise版を評価し、 アクセス制御とOpenAIのビジネスデータ学習除外ポリシーを確認した上で導入を決めています。 日本への影響・ビジネス活用のヒント この事例が示す重要なポイントは、 使用頻度が上がるほどROIが大幅に増加する という点です。 月あたりの推定ROIが55%だったものが101回以上の利用で524%に跳ね上がることは、 AIツールを「たまに使う」のではなく「日常的に使いこなす」ことの重要性を示しています。 単に導入するだけでなく、社員が日常業務でAIを使いこなせる環境・研修・文化を整えることが、 投資対効果を最大化する鍵になると見られます（推測）。 また、金融機関というセキュリティ要件の厳しい業種でも、 ChatGPT EnterpriseのデータポリシーとアクセスコントロールでAI活用が実現できることが示されました。 中小企業においても、セキュリティへの懸念を整理した上でAI導入を進めることが可能です。 久留米・福岡の中小企業様への活用提案 住友生命の事例は大企業の話ですが、久留米・福岡の中小企業にも直接活かせる示唆があります。 使用頻度が高いほどROIが上がるという法則は企業規模に関わらず同じです。 たとえば、久留米の製造業で見積書・仕様書の作成に毎日AIを使うスタッフと、 週1回しか使わないスタッフでは、業務短縮効果に大きな差が生まれます。 導入後の社内研修・使い方の共有・活用ルール整備が、ROIを左右する最重要ポイントです。 福岡の士業・コンサルティング・不動産業などでは、 顧客向け文書作成・契約書ドラフト・資料まとめといった作業がAIで大幅に効率化できます。 月に何十回もAIを使う習慣が根付けば、スタッフ1人あたり月数時間〜十数時間の工数削減が期待でき、 年間数十万円規模のコスト削減効果につながると見られます（規模・業種による推測）。 ヒカリのAIスクール・AI導入支援では、単にツールを入れて終わりではなく、 久留米・福岡の中小企業の現場スタッフが日常的にAIを使いこなすまでの定着支援を重視しています。 住友生命の事例のように、使い込むほど効果が出る仕組みを、御社の規模に合わせてご一緒に作ります。 AIの活用についてご相談はこちら →

records.label: finance.biggo.com
records.title: OpenAI Rolls Out Private Inference to Win Enterprise Clients, but GPT-6.2 Billing Fix Speeds Users' Quota Depletion by 40%
records.excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman unveiled a private inference mode paired with a Zero Data Retention (ZDR) mechanism, under which data is erased once processed and OpenAI staff cannot access the original content, aimed squarely at large enterprise clients in finance, healthcare and other sectors highly sensitive to data leaks. At the same time, technical lead Tibo Sottiaux acknowledged a usage-billing error during the GPT-6.2 rollout; after the fix, users doing the same work hit their quota limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol. OpenAI pledged not to claw back historical shortfalls and offered paying users a one-time quota reset. The developer community criticized the tightening of quotas coinciding with a decline in model reasoning tokens, arguing the company is shifting resources toward enterprise customers.

records.title: OpenAI Plans Shared Quota for ChatGPT and Codex
records.excerpt: OpenAI Plans Shared Quota for ChatGPT and Codex — Brief AI Partner GenerationAI Paris, December 1 and 2 GenerationAI Paris, December 1 and 2 80+ speakers, from OpenAI to Anthropic: the €1,199 VIP invitation is on us. Free VIP invitation Free VIP invitation → Brief AI › OpenAI Plans Shared Quota for ChatGPT and Codex AI Tools · Tom Levy · November 28, 2026 OpenAI Plans Shared Quota for ChatGPT and Codex Key Takeaways 1 OpenAI plans to implement a shared allocation for ChatGPT and Codex starting in December for Plus, Pro, and Business users. 2 According to OpenAI, Enterprise is not affected by this change. 3 The company states that instant chat will remain outside of the shared allocation. Why it matters : the consumption of one service will reduce the resources available for the other, with a risk of faster depletion for heavy users. OpenAI plans to share the same allocation between ChatGPT and Codex starting in December for Plus, Pro, and Business subscriptions. Intensive usage could deplete their available resources more quickly, but instant chat should remain accessible outside of this quota. Enterprise is exempt from the quota change According to OpenAI, the Enterprise offering will not be affected by this change. Organizations whose employees heavily rely on its services can therefore consider this subscription. However, its price is neither public nor fixed: a pricing proposal can be obtained from OpenAI's sales team. This choice requires comparing the expected benefits to the actual amount proposed. File photo: Reuters OpenAI is suing Apple, accusing the tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on its planned devices, after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology. It filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple's employment practices were designed to "trap" employees and prevent them from working on competitors' technology. OpenAI, whose ChatGPT is integrated into some generations of iPhones, is developing AI-enabled personal electronic devices that threaten to "outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf", the company said in its Friday court filing. OpenAI said in the filing that Apple gained confidential information by rehiring a former employee who worked at OpenAI for six months. In that time, the employee gained access to specific information on a new device as well as OpenAI's roadmap for future hardware products. "Given the timing, it now appears that stealing those documents may have been his reason for joining OpenAI in the first place," it said. Apple denied using the rehired employee to access OpenAI's confidential information and denied trying to suppress competition in AI device manufacturing. "OpenAI’s counterclaims are a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple’s lawsuit," Apple said. Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology. Apple sued OpenAI and former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu in July, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner's foray into consumer hardware. Tan, a 24-year Apple employee who had been a vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch, was part of the group that launched the AI device startup io Products before it was acquired by OpenAI in 2025. OpenAI and the employees have denied those allegations and said that Apple's lawsuit depended on its unauthorized monitoring of Liu's personal messages after he stopped working for Apple. In Friday's filing, OpenAI criticised Apple for encouraging employees to do work on their personal Apple devices and accounts, then preventing those employees from an orderly separation of work and personal accounts when they leave for new jobs. OpenAI said that Apple continues to access former employees' personal devices and accounts after they leave the company, enabling Apple to "monitor and ensnare departing employees" when they leave for competitors. OpenAI said that 400 employees have left Apple for OpenAI so far, and Apple wants to intimidate other employees from leaving to find other tech companies.
