records.title: Honda、FIA Road Safety Indexで世界初の5スターを獲得
records.excerpt: Honda、FIA Road Safety Indexで世界初の5スターを獲得 | Honda Stories | Honda 企業情報サイト HONDA The Power of Dreams HONDA The Power of Dreams トップ 新着記事 タグ メールマガジン × 経営 2026.11.27 Honda、FIA Road Safety Indexで世界初の5スターを獲得 #安全・運転支援 #クルマ #バイク 「Safety for Everyone すべての人の安全をめざして」という考えのもと、Hondaは、クルマやバイクに乗っている人だけでなく、道を使う誰もが安全でいられる「事故に遭わない社会」の実現を目指しています。 その実現に向けて、Hondaは、2050年に全世界でHondaの二輪車・四輪車が関与する交通事故死者ゼロを目指し、2030年には交通事故死者半減をマイルストーンと位置付けています。 こうした目標を掲げ、Hondaは「人の能力（啓発活動）」「モビリティの性能（技術開発）」「交通エコシステム（協働、システム／サービス開発）」という3つの要素をそれぞれ進化させ、組み合わせながら、安全への取り組みを進めています。 これらの安全への取り組みを世界各地で積み重ねてきたHondaは、FIA（国際自動車連盟）が定める企業・団体の交通安全への取り組み評価指標「FIA Road Safety Index」の製品・サービスの安全関連評価において、世界で初めて最高ランクとなる「5スター」を獲得しました。 FIA Road Safety Indexとは 2022年に始まったFIA Road Safety Indexは、定量・定性の両面のエビデンスに基づき企業の交通安全に関する取り組みを評価するものです。企業活動が環境に与える影響を測る取り組みと同様に、企業の事業活動に伴う交通事故による死亡・負傷の「フットプリント ※1 」を評価し、その低減につなげることを目的としています。 ※1 企業・団体の事業活動に伴う交通事故による死亡・負傷の規模。製品・サービスやサプライチェーンを含めて推計・把握し、交通安全に与える影響を可視化するもの。 審査を受けることで、企業は自社の製品やサービス、サプライチェーンが交通安全に与える影響を把握し、改善すべき点をより明確にすることができます。より安全で持続可能なモビリティ社会という世界共通の目標に向け、企業が交通安全の成果に対して果たすべき責任を明確にする指標として位置づけられています。 Hondaは、自動車メーカーとして初めてFIA Road Safety Indexの審査を受け、2025年には当時の最高評価である「3スター」を獲得しました。審査では、Hondaの幅広い事業活動を対象に、ESG（環境・社会・ガバナンス）レポートをはじめ、バリューチェーン全体における交通事故による死者数・重傷者数、社内の交通安全に関する規定、安全教育や啓発活動など、さまざまな項目が評価されました。 Hondaが最高評価を獲得 2025年、FIAはFIA Road Safety Indexの評価範囲を拡大し、「計画」「安全パフォーマンスのモニタリング」「安全文化のマネジメントおよびサプライチェーンまたは製品・サービスのカバー範囲」という3つの評価項目を新たに導入しました。これにより、最高評価は従来の3スターから5スターへと引き上げられました ※2 。 ※2 2025年2月改訂のFIA Road Safety Index評価手法（Products and Services Manual）に基づく この変更について、FIAで自動車モビリティ、サステナビリティ、ツーリズム担当事務総長を務めるウィレム・グルーネワルド氏は、次のように説明しています。 「FIA Road Safety Indexを5スターへと拡張したことは、交通安全を企業の意思決定において測定可能で、責任の所在が明確なものにしていくという私たちの目標に向けた重要な一歩です。評価手法の拡充によって、企業は自らが交通安全に与える影響をより広く把握できるだけでなく、目標を設定し、進捗を確認し、具体的な取り組みを示しながら、継続的に改善していくことができます」 Hondaは今回、新たな評価項目への対応を含め、FIAによる審査対象を17カ国へと拡大しました。対象となったのは、日本、米国、英国、フランス、ドイツ、イタリア、スペイン、トルコ、中国、タイ、ベトナム、インドネシア、マレーシア、インド、パキスタン、フィリピン、ブラジルで、これらの国を合わせると、Hondaの二輪車・四輪車の世界販売台数の90％以上を占めます。 Hondaの5スター獲得の背景には、経営層が参画しながら、中長期的な戦略に基づいて安全への取り組みを推進していることがあります。また、サステナビリティガバナンスの一環として、グローバルの安全に関する会議体が安全目標の達成に向けた進捗をモニタリングしていることも評価されました。 さらにFIAは、Hondaが先進安全技術を積極的に活用していることに加え、全社を挙げて安全文化の醸成に取り組んでいる点を評価しました。安全への取り組みに「Plan（計画）」「Do（実行）」「Check（評価）」「Act（改善）」からなるPDCAサイクルを確立していることも高く評価されています。このPDCAの考え方によって、Hondaは安全に関する取り組みを継続的に改善しています。 安全運転普及本部の小嶋幹人（こじまみきひと）事務局長は、今回の5スター評価について次のようにコメントしています。 小嶋 今回、5スターの評価をいただけたことを大変光栄に思います。 Hondaは、Honda製品をお使いいただくお客様一人ひとりの安全はもちろん、道を使う誰もが安全でいられる「事故に遭わない社会」を目指しています。FIA Road Safety Indexは、企業による交通安全への取り組みを可視化するものであり、Hondaが現在どの位置にいるのか、そして次に何に取り組むべきなのかを、より明確にする機会となりました。 今回の評価を、2050年に全世界でHondaの二輪車・四輪車が関与する交通事故死者ゼロという高い目標を実現するための、重要なマイルストーンの一つと捉えています。 いいね 共有する Facebookでシェア Xで投稿する records.excerpt: FIA confirms Qatar Grand Prix decision after press conference breach FIA reaches Sergio Perez decision after Qatar GP press conference delay Oliver Harden 27 Nov 2026 7:21 PM Sergio Perez faced the media alone in Qatar after arriving late to a press conference Cadillac driver Sergio Perez has avoided a penalty after arriving late to Thursday’s FIA press conference at the Qatar Grand Prix, it has been announced. Perez had been scheduled to appear in the second part of Thursday’s FIA drivers’ press conference in Qatar along with Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri. Sergio Perez escapes FIA penalty after late arrival to Qatar GP press conference However, the Mexican driver arrived late to the media briefing, with Leclerc and Piastri left to face questions between them. Perez eventually arrived after Piastri and Leclerc had left, leaving the Cadillac racer to field questions alone. Following a hearing on Friday, the FIA stewards have confirmed that Perez will face no action. Sergio Perez vs Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates The stewards explained that Perez was delayed by “two circumstances beyond his control” with an insurance issue resulting in a delay to his flight to Qatar before road closures slowed him down further. The stewards’ verdict read: “The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 11 (Sergio Perez), and the Team Representative. “The driver conceded that he was 22 minutes late for the Press Conference, however he explained that this was caused by two circumstances beyond his control. “The first related to an insurance issue which resulted in his flight to Doha being delayed such that he landed only one hour prior to the scheduled start time for the Conference. “Normally this would have allowed him sufficient time to meet his commitment, however on approach to the circuit, he was held up by several road closures. “The Stewards note that other parties were likewise held up on arrival at the circuit due to similar circumstances. “The team advised that it had kept the FIA Media Delegate informed of the delay. “Accordingly, although this is a breach of the regulations, in view of the circumstances, no penalty is applied.” More on Sergio Perez and Cadillac from PlanetF1.com Sergio Perez news Cadillac news The decision to take no further action against Perez comes despite Ferrari and McLaren receiving suspended fines after Leclerc and Lando Norris were late to press conferences in Monaco earlier this year. McLaren and Ferrari were both given suspended fines of €5,000 in Monte Carlo in June after Norris and Leclerc arrived within minutes of the press conference starting. Perez was classified in last place in Friday’s second practice session in Qatar, trailing Cadillac teammate Valtteri Bottas by a tenth. Cadillac, the first new team to arrive in F1 since fellow US outfit Haas in 2016, is yet to score a point in its debut season. Bottas recorded the team’s best result at the second round in China in March, finishing 13th. records.title: Red Bull learn fate as FIA concludes investigation into Hadjar incident
records.excerpt: The FIA stewards have delivered their verdict on Red Bull Racing following an incident involving Isack Hadjar during the opening free practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix. The incident occurred du... The FIA stewards have delivered their verdict on Red Bull Racing following an incident involving Isack Hadjar during the opening free practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix. Red Bull learn fate as FIA concludes investigation into Hadjar incident Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Breaking News 17:46, 27 Nov 2 Comments Tobia Elia Tobia is a Formula 1 journalist at GPblog with experience at international circuits. Since 2022, he has covered Grands Prix across Europe, delivering reliable coverage and insights from the paddock. The FIA stewards have delivered their verdict on Red Bull Racing following an incident involving Isack Hadjar during the opening free practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix. The incident occurred during FP1 , when Hadjar began pulling away from his pit box before a Red Bull mechanic had finished working on his car, prompting an investigation by the stewards. The team was subsequently held responsible for the incident. FIA explains Red Bull penalty after Hadjar incident According to the stewards' findings, the incident stemmed from a procedural error within the Red Bull garage. A new member of the team placed a cooling blower on the left rear brakes of Hadjar's car, despite this not being part of the team's usual procedure. As a result, the process of releasing Hadjar onto the track began before the mechanic had the opportunity to fully remove the equipment. As the Frenchman pulled away, part of the blower remained in place, while the mechanic's foot came into contact with the left rear wheel of the RB22. ADVERTISEMENT The stewards highlighted the potential consequences of the incident, stressing that it could have resulted in an injury to the mechanic. They also emphasised that the safety of team personnel must remain a priority regardless of whether an incident occurs during a practice session or a race. Photo: Race Pictures Red Bull acknowledged that the incident was the result of an error in their procedures, with the stewards stating that the financial penalty was consistent with those handed out for similar incidents in recent years. The Milton Keynes-based outfit will therefore have to pay €10,000 immediately, with the remaining €20,000 only coming into effect should the team commit another breach of the same article within the next 12 months. Hadjar himself has escaped any sporting penalty after finishing the opening practice session in third place, behind the Mercedes duo of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell. records.excerpt: Red Bull explains Isack Hadjar pit lane incident that led to FIA punishment Michelle Foster & Thomas Maher 28 Nov 2026 8:53 AM Red Bull copped a fine in Qatar Red Bull technical director Pierre Waché has explained that it was an error from a new mechanic that led to Isack Hadjar ’s pit lane incident in FP1 for the Qatar Grand Prix. Red Bull copped a fine after Hadjar accidentally ran over one of his mechanic’s feet as he was still working on the Frenchman’s RB22. Pierre Waché explains Isack Hadjar’s Red Bull pit lane incident Hadjar pitted during FP1, with four of his mechanics quickly blasting cold air onto his brakes. But as he pulled away from the pit box, the mechanic on his rear left did not step back in time with the other three as he continued to blow air on the rear left brake. He got caught out, with Hadjar not only breaking the air blower but also running over the mechanic’s foot. Hitting the brakes, Hadjar asked: “Is everyone okay?” He was reassured by his race engineer, Richard Wood saying: “Yeah, okay mate. All okay.” The incident was investigated by the stewards who determined that Red Bull had breached Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code, which concerns safety procedures in the pit lane. The team was handed a fine of €30,000, €20,000 of which has been suspended for 12 months, subject to there being no further breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code. Technical director Waché explained that it was an error on the part of a new mechanic. “Yeah, it’s a type of pit stop that you are not maybe, when you are new, taking the same caution of,” Waché told PlanetF1.com and other accredited media. “Unfortunately, you know, brake cooling at the time was not the main problem, and it happened.” F1 2026: The season’s winners and losers The results of the F1 2026 championship The F1 2026 Drivers’ and Constructors’ Championship standings Hadjar finished Friday’s running with the sixth-fastest time, lining up behind Max Verstappen on the timesheet, with Red Bull half a second down on the pace set by Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli. Both Hadjar and Verstappen struggled with the balance of their RB22s, with Waché saying Red Bull needed to resolve that before the team could even think about chasing down Mercedes. “I think it’s key to fix the balance issue that we can have here by having a massive front limitation in the high-speed and medium-speed corners without compromising the corner entry,” he said. “They [Mercedes] are able to do that and we have work to do to achieve that.” Asked if Red Bull could turn it around overnight as the team has often done in the past, the Frenchman admitted he wasn’t sure given Mercedes’ pace advantage on Friday. “No, but I think that’s just what I feel. It doesn’t mean what we will achieve [it],” he said. “I hope that we will achieve the same turnaround as normal, but I don’t feel that we… The gap is big. The gap is very big and that makes it difficult for us to achieve that.” Read next: Lance Stroll reveals cause of back injury suffered in Qatar practice Red Bull Isack Hadjar

records.excerpt: FIA makes key decision ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Jamie Woodhouse 26 Nov 2026 7:00 AM The FIA is Formula 1's governing body The FIA has confirmed that four straight-mode zones will be in place at the Lusail International Circuit for this week’s Qatar Grand Prix. Active aero in part replaced the former DRS system under the new rules for the F1 2026 season. FIA confirms four SM zones for Qatar Grand Prix Straight Mode allows drivers to open and close their rear wings at different parts of each track. Straight Mode is designed to help reduce drag on the straights. The cars return to their standard configuration of closed front and rear wings for maximum downforce in the corners. The number of SM zones has varied at each circuit in 2026. Active aero was effectively banned at the Monaco Grand Prix in June, due to the tight and twisty nature of the Monte Carlo Circuit. The FIA has confirmed that four Straight Mode zones will be in use at the Qatar Grand Prix around the Lusail International Circuit. A first dose will be available shortly after drivers exit the final corner, Turn 16, running down the the start/finish straight. Drivers will get SM again for the straight between Turns 3 and 4. The racers will then need to wait under Sector 2 for Straight Mode to return. It can be activated out of Turn 10 and through the almost-straight that is Turn 11. The wings must return to the normal configuration on approach to Turn 12, which marks the start of a series of sweeping right-handers. One final SM zone comes on the straight between Turns 15 and 16, meaning the F1 2026 stars will not have long to wait before re-joining the main straight and picking SM back up. The detection point for Overtake Mode is positioned coming out of T16, followed shortly after by the activation point, giving drivers within one second of the car ahead that extra 0.5MJ of power to play with. Latest F1 2026 talking points on PlanetF1.com Max Verstappen issues ‘rather stay at home’ verdict on F1 Middle East finale Lewis Hamilton accused of ‘deliberate’ act in Leclerc Las Vegas crash Lusail is one of the most demanding tracks which Formula 1 visits with its relentless high-speed corners. It is the kind of circuit which gives the Pirelli tyres nightmares. Qatar marks part one of a Middle East double-header, alongside Abu Dhabi, which brings F1 2026 to its conclusion. It follows a period of uncertainty over Formula 1 returning to the region, due to the ongoing conflict. Ultimately, the backup option of Imola was stood down, as Formula 1 committed to the Qatar and Abu Dhabi rounds. records.excerpt: FIA confirms final decision as Audi F1 team loses Yuki Tsunoda appeal FIA confirms final decision as Audi F1 team loses Yuki Tsunoda appeal Oliver Harden 27 Nov 2026 5:42 PM Yuki Tsunoda will keep his 10th place from the Italian Grand Prix after Audi's appeal was rejected The Audi F1 team has lost its appeal against Yuki Tsunoda’s 10th-place finish at the Italian Grand Prix, the FIA has announced. Tsunoda collected the final point for 10th place at Monza at the start of September during his three-race cameo with the Racing Bulls team. Audi loses FIA appeal against Yuki Tsunoda Italian GP result The Japanese driver’s points finish came after Tsunoda was involved in a mix-up while lining up on the grid. Tsunoda had been due to start 14th, but initially went to line up on the opposite side of the grid in 15th. With Tsunoda’s car at a strange angle on the grid, the FIA’s Formula 1 race director Rui Marques opted to signal an additional formation lap. Audi, whose drivers Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg finished behind Tsunoda in 11th and 12th respectively, went on to challenge the result with an appeal. Nico Hulkenberg vs Gabriel Bortoleto: Audi head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates The Swiss-based team argued that Tsunoda should have been penalised for triggering an extra formation lap. However, Tsunoda was not deemed to be the cause of the additional formation lap, with the stewards opting against penalising the Racing Bulls driver on the day. The stewards at Monza wrote that Marques himself took the decision for an extra formation lap having “stated he was not comfortable starting the race with the car in that position.” Following a hearing in Paris on Wednesday, the FIA’s International Court of Appeal has rejected Audi’s case. The decision means Tsunoda will be allowed to keep his 10th place. An FIA statement read: “On 6 September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the Race Director ordered an additional formation lap. “Following the race, the Stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (Driver of Car No. 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. “Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the Driver. In Decision No. 69, the Stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. “On 9 September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty. “The Court, after having heard the parties and examined their submissions, decided to: “Declare the appeal admissible; “Dismiss the appeal on the merits; “Uphold the Decision No. 69 of the Stewards of the 2026 Italian Grand Prix, dated 6 September 2026, counting towards the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship; “And order the competent Sporting Authority to draw, as appropriate, the consequences of this ruling. “The International Court of Appeal was presided over by Mr Laurent Anselmi (Monaco), and included, Mr Mark Kletter (Austria), Mr Philip Moser (United Kingdom) and Mr Laurent Nuss (France). “The full decision will be available at a later date.” In a statement issued to PlanetF1.com in response to the decision, Audi said: “We are deeply surprised with the outcome and will study the full ruling in greater depth when it is shared.” Read next: F1 takes unprecedented action ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Racing Bulls FIA Yuki Tsunoda Related Articles Oliver Harden 27 Nov 2026 FIA reaches Sergio Perez decision after Qatar GP press conference delay Sergio Perez's explanation has come to light. records.excerpt: Lance Stroll reveals cause of back injury suffered in Qatar practice Michelle Foster 28 Nov 2026 7:38 AM Lance Stroll hurt his back in FP2 in Qatar Aston Martin driver Lance Stroll has revealed he “tweaked” his lower back during Friday’s second practice session for the Qatar Grand Prix, leaving him in pain. Stroll had an eventful Friday at the Lusail circuit as he suffered a notable off in both practice sessions. Lance Stroll reveals lower back injury during Qatar GP practice The Canadian had a big moment in FP1 as he rode the kerbs and kicked up gravel and dust, which led to Alex Albon, who was behind him, doing the same. Stroll was again off the track in the night session as he understeered at Turn 2. He finished 20th in both practices and ended the night 3.571s off the pace set by Kimi Antonelli on what proved to be a trying Friday for Aston Martin. “It was difficult,” Stroll told PlanetF1.com and other accredited media, before revealing his back injury. “It’s a different track to Las Vegas, and [I was] trying to put the car in a good window for this track. “And then [I was] dealing with some back pain in the second session, so that was also really tricky. “I just tweaked my lower back in the second session, so I’m just battling that.” Asked if the injury could “compromise” him for the rest of the weekend, Stroll replied: “We’re going to see. “I’m going to try and work on it and do what I can tonight, but it was bothering me a lot.” Stroll refuted the suggestion that his injury was caused by his two big offs, instead saying it was the result of the G-forces experienced in the high-speed final sector of the track. “It wasn’t actually in one of those offs,” he insisted. “It was just in the last sector, in the right-hand corner, it has just tweaked the lower back with the G-forces. “So try to get on top of it tonight.” Fernando Alonso vs Lance Stroll: Aston Martin F1 2026 scores F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Should Stroll be unable to continue in Qatar, Aston Martin could call up junior driver Jak Crawford. records.excerpt: FIA confirms Lewis Hamilton decision after Max Verstappen Qatar GP incident Jamie Woodhouse 27 Nov 2026 6:56 PM Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen: the best of enemies The FIA stewards decided to take no further action against Lewis Hamilton following an incident involving Max Verstappen in FP2 at the Qatar Grand Prix. The moment in question occurred during the second hour of practice around the Lusail International Circuit down the main straight and into Turn 1. Hamilton’s movement into the braking zone alerted Verstappen and the stewards, but it was deemed that matters did not need to be taken any further. Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen escape FIA action Following the saga from Las Vegas which had Verstappen and George Russell back at each other’s throats, the Dutchman may have felt a sense of deja vu in Qatar. During Friday’s FP2 session, Verstappen passed Hamilton’s Ferrari down the start/finish straight, only for the Brit to move back past the Red Bull approaching Turn 1. Hamilton , now on the outside, appeared to cut quite sharply across Verstappen into T1 to take the optimal racing line. Contact was avoided. “Ah. You saw that under braking? My God,” said Verstappen over team radio in response to that moment. Hamilton’s stance on the radio was: “I got traffic with Max.” The FIA stewards noted the Ferrari driver for potential erratic driving. With FP2 still in progress, the decision came through that no further action would be taken. Verstappen went on to finish FP2 in fifth, while for Hamilton it was eighth. Despite being cleared by the stewards, Hamilton’s dramas did not end there. In the closing moments of the session, he was forced to park his Ferrari in the gravel out of T1. “I’ve lost the engine,” he reported. Told by Ferrari to stop the car, the seven-time world champion confirmed that it had stopped itself. This triggered a Virtual Safety Car which brought FP2 to its conclusion, a session which left questions unanswered as to the true state of the pecking order. Latest Qatar Grand Prix news on PlanetF1.com F1 engine freeze confirmed as V8 transition plans revealed FIA confirms final decision as Audi F1 team loses Yuki Tsunoda appeal Kimi Antonelli topped the session in a Mercedes one-two, despite neither he nor George Russell having completed a lap on the soft tyres. Russell had gone purple in the first two sectors on that red-walled compound, but was forced to abort when the red flag was triggered, either for gravel on track after a spin for Hamilton’s Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc, or a piece of debris later deposited by his SF-26. Neither Ferrari completed a representative lap on the softs either. In addition to that red flag, and the VSC triggered by Hamilton, there was a further red flag headache for the drivers caused by Pierre Gasly’s spin into the gravel approaching Turn 14, where his Alpine became beached. FP2 was ultimately extended by 13 minutes, as the FIA took action on the various interruptions throughout that session. In the end, Antonelli completed the Friday clean sweep, topping FP1 and FP2 from Russell in a strong start to the race weekend from Mercedes. records.excerpt: Kimi Antonelli reveals major concern for Qatar Grand Prix Sam Hall 27 Nov 2026 8:04 PM Antonelli has a major concern in Qatar Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has revealed a significant concern over front tyre pressures at the Qatar Grand Prix after struggling to control wear in Friday practice. Antonelli topped both sessions at Lusail on Friday, but it was far from smooth sailing. Kimi Antonelli voices tyre pressure concerns at Qatar Grand Prix Tyres have been a major talking point ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix weekend, just as has been the case on each visit to the Lusail International Circuit to date. The track is a relentless path of high- and medium-speed corners, with hugely aggressive kerbs, and little in the way of low-speed sections to allow the tyres any respite. Due to the continual extreme forces, Pirelli has routinely mandated a maximum distance that tyres can be taken, with this figure steadily increasing from 18 laps in 2023, when the biggest concern was the kerbs. For the 2026 running, drivers can complete a maximum of 27 laps on each set of tyres, with this number including laps in and out of the pits, as well as any laps completed under full or virtual safety car conditions. Further, this total per tyre set is cumulative across all sessions, so practice and qualifying running must also be factored in. With the race being 57 laps long, this means that teams are forced to run a two-stop strategy. However, things became even more restrictive ahead of FP1, as the FIA mandated a minimum front tyre pressure of 29psi. The previous benchmark for minimum front-tyre pressures in the F1 2026 season was 28psi, which was in place in Japan (Suzuka), Britain (Silverstone) and Belgium (Spa). This equals the requirement from last year, which was increased from an initial 28psi after cuts were found in the tyres on Friday. Antonelli topped both sessions on Friday despite failing to complete a qualifying simulation lap on soft tyres in either outing, and hopes that the pressures will not be increased further as the weekend progresses. “They’re very high and let’s see if tomorrow they’re going to do an even further step; hopefully not,” he said of the high tyre pressures. “But definitely, the front left is the one that is suffering the most out there and it’s really easy to wear it out completely. “So just need to be on top of it and try to find the right balance as well for the race. “But then I think also qualifying tomorrow is going to be very important to qualify as far in front as possible in order to have a better chance to win the race.” More Qatar Grand Prix news from PlanetF1.com FIA confirms Lewis Hamilton decision after Max Verstappen Qatar GP incident Red Bull fined by FIA after Isack Hadjar incident triggers Qatar GP investigation In FP1, an error from Antonelli cost him a lap on soft tyres, while a pair of red flag interruptions in FP2, which ultimately saw the session extended by 13 minutes, hampered both he and teammate George Russell in the latter running. Despite this, Antonelli said: “It felt good. I think the car has been feeling strong overall, although there’s still lots of work to do. “But all in all, I think we can be happy with today. We got a lot of understanding and just need to work overnight to come back with hopefully some changes that will improve the car even further. “On my side, I will try to see where I can do better and be ready for tomorrow.” Read more: Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli tops FP2 amid Ferrari drama Mercedes Kimi Antonelli

records.excerpt: Qatar GP: Ferrari dramas as Kimi Antonelli tops FP2 Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli tops FP2 amid Ferrari drama Jamie Woodhouse 27 Nov 2026 6:17 PM Lewis Hamilton in action for Ferrari Kimi Antonelli completed the clean sweep on Friday at the Qatar Grand Prix, FP2 proving a highly eventful session. The FIA opted to extend FP2 by 13 minutes following a pair of red flag interruptions, while there was a spin for Charles Leclerc and a late stoppage for Lewis Hamilton who lost the engine in his sister Ferrari. Neither Antonelli nor Mercedes teammate George Russell got a representative soft-tyre lap in due to the various incidents. Kimi Antonelli tops eventful Qatar GP FP2 Antonelli and Mercedes was the combination to beat heading into the second hour of practice. The world champion elect had headed a one-two by half a second from George Russell. Drivers had widely struggled to piece together a lap on the soft tyres, making that a significant point of focus for FP2. As was the case earlier in the day, it was the medium tyres in demand at the start of this second practice session. Antonelli’s opening effort was a 1:23.807, quickly bettered by Russell by just under a tenth. There was an early spin through the gravel at Turn 9 for Charles Leclerc. The Ferrari man was potentially distracted by the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson returning to the track, albeit well off the racing line. “The car is not feeling okay,” the Monegasque reported soon after. He returned to the garage and hopped out of his Ferrari. No such troubles for Russell, who found the better part of another four-tenths. Antonelli swiftly struck back, going a quarter of a second clear with the pace upped to a 1:23.077. “The car is very unstable, very on the nose,” Lewis Hamilton reported, adding that he had no rear anywhere around the track. He was down in seventh, over a second off the pace. As the session approached halfway, Red Bull bolted on the softs for a qualifying simulation. Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar improved, but not enough to trouble the Mercedes pair. McLaren could not trouble the Mercs either upon the switch to those red-walled tyres. Russell got a handy tow from Fernando Alonso’s Aston Martin as he set off on a soft lap. After two purple sectors, red flag. Potentially, for gravel on the track through Turns 7/8. It may also have been for a piece of debris at Turn 12, deposited by Leclerc’s Ferrari after his earlier spin. The track was back to green with a little under half an hour to go. It was soon back to red flag conditions. Pierre Gasly’s Alpine was beached in the gravel approaching Turn 14. Latest Qatar Grand Prix talking points on PlanetF1.com F1 takes unprecedented action ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton reveals plan to ‘shoot the s**t’ with Leclerc over Ferrari differences There was 15 minutes left on the clock as FP2 resumed. Considering the awkward timings of those red flags, there was a mixture of run plans. The Ferraris, both of them, were back out on softs. Mediums on the Mercedes, Red Bulls and McLarens. Word then came through from the FIA that the session had been extended by 13 minutes. Hamilton and Verstappen went side-by-side down the main straight, the latter not happy with how the Ferrari appeared to cut across into the braking zone. Hamilton was noted by the FIA stewards over potential erratic driving. No further action was the verdict. Lance Stroll’s Aston Martin understeered off the road at Turn 2, the pack now focusing on race simulation. Russell witnessed a near-miss between Carlos Sainz and Franco Colapinto into the first corner, as Gasly’s sister Alpine arrived back in pit-lane. There were further dramas for Hamilton. “I’ve lost the engine.” Virtual Safety Car as he climbed out of his stricken Ferrari, parked out of T1. That VSC brought the session to its end, Antonelli on top from Russell despite the Mercedes pair not getting a soft-tyre lap in. records.excerpt: FIA launches Qatar Grand Prix investigation over press conference breach FIA launches Sergio Perez investigation over Qatar GP press conference breach Oliver Harden 26 Nov 2026 6:06 PM Sergio Perez sits alone in the FIA press conference in Qatar after arriving late Cadillac driver Sergio Perez is under investigation by the FIA stewards after arriving late to Thursday’s press conference at the Qatar Grand Prix. The penultimate race of the F1 2026 season will take place at the Lusail circuit in Qatar. Sergio Perez under FIA investigation after late press conference arrival Thursday’s media activities routinely see six drivers appear across two FIA press conference sessions. The first session on Thursday saw Haas driver Oliver Bearman, Mercedes’ George Russell and Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar face questions from the media. Perez was expected to join Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri for the second part of the session in Qatar. However, Perez failed to appear for the duration of the second press conference with Leclerc and Piastri left to field questions. Having arrived late, Perez faced the media alone after Leclerc and Piastri had left the room. PlanetF1.com understands that Perez’s plane was late arriving in Qatar, leading to his initial absence from the press conference. Sergio Perez vs Valtteri Bottas: Cadillac head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Following the press conference, the FIA has confirmed that Perez has been summoned to the stewards for arriving late to the press briefing. Perez and a Cadillac team representative are required to report to the stewards at 18:30 local time on Friday in Qatar. The hearing will take place 30 minutes after the conclusion of the second practice session at Lusail. Perez’s late appearance comes after Leclerc and Lando Norris were both put under investigation for being late to the Thursday FIA press conference at June’s Monaco Grand Prix. Ferrari and McLaren were both given suspended fines of €5,000 on that occasion after Leclerc and Norris arrived within moments of the press conference starting. The fact that Perez missed the entirety of the second session, forcing an extra session featuring him alone, could leave the Mexican driver and Cadillac in line for a harsher punishment. More on Sergio Perez and Cadillac from PlanetF1.com Sergio Perez news Cadillac news Cadillac enters the Qatar Grand Prix still searching for its first point of the F1 2026 season. The US team remains at the foot of the championship table, with Valtteri Bottas’s 13th place at the second race in China still Cadillac’s best result of its debut season. Perez, a six-time race winner in F1, came close to securing Cadillac’s first-ever point in Monaco before a post-race time penalty dropped him to 15th in the final classification. Cadillac announced last month that Perez, who will turn 37 in January, will remain with the team until at least the end of the 2029 season after signing a new long-term contract. Bottas found his seat under threat from the likes of test driver Colton Herta and Mercedes reserve Fred Vesti. However, the team ended weeks of speculation in Las Vegas last weekend by confirming that Bottas will remain with the team for the F1 2027 campaign. records.excerpt: Wednesday's Formula 1 headlines focus on the FIA's financial regulations, Aston Martin's ongoing struggles with Honda, and the growing tension between Max Verstappen and George Russell ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix News Summary Williams faces financial and sporting penalties after exceeding the 2025 cost cap, while Alpine is also sanctioned for a reporting breach. Fernando Alonso admits Aston Martin cannot compete with its rivals under the current Honda power unit , raising questions about the team’s prospects. Max Verstappen and George Russell remain at the centre of F1’s latest rivalry , with the Qatar Grand Prix approaching. Williams accepts FIA penalty after cost cap breach Williams has accepted a financial penalty and a sporting sanction after exceeding Formula 1’s 2025 cost cap by £627,000 (0.48%) . The FIA classified the case as a minor overspend accompanied by a procedural breach. The team will also face a 1.5% reduction in wind tunnel and CFD testing over the next 12 months . Williams attributed the issue to administrative expenses related to changes in its corporate structure. The team stressed that the FIA found no sporting or financial advantage resulting from the breach. The decision comes at a difficult time for the Grove-based outfit, which is looking to strengthen its competitiveness ahead of the next development cycle. Alonso points to Honda deficit as Aston Martin struggles Fernando Alonso has once again highlighted the limitations of Aston Martin’s Honda power unit following a difficult weekend in Las Vegas. The Spaniard believes the engine remains significantly behind its rivals in both performance and reliability, preventing the team from fighting for better results. Despite the concerns, Alonso sees potential for improvement through chassis development and hopes the team can make progress ahead of the 2027 season. The comments add pressure on Aston Martin and Honda as the partnership prepares for another crucial stage in its development Verstappen and Russell rivalry heats up before Qatar The tension between Max Verstappen and George Russell remains one of the main talking points following the Las Vegas Grand Prix . The Red Bull driver has continued his verbal attacks on Russell after their latest confrontation, reviving a rivalry that dates back to 2024. Verstappen arrives in Qatar after winning four of the last six races and remains a strong contender for second place in the Drivers’ Championship. He has also won the last three editions of the Qatar Grand Prix. Russell, meanwhile, is looking to recover after another difficult weekend, with Mercedes having missed the podium in consecutive races. Max Verstappen has continued his verbal attacks on Russell after their latest confrontation (Photo: Red Bull Content Pool) Audi appeal could give Bortoleto an extra point The FIA’s International Court of Appeal is scheduled to hear Audi’s challenge over the stewards’ decision at the Italian Grand Prix. The case concerns Yuki Tsunoda and an additional formation lap at Monza. Audi argues that the Racing Bulls driver should have received a penalty. A successful appeal could change the final classification and promote Gabriel Bortoleto from 11th to tenth, giving the Brazilian an additional championship point. The hearing takes place in Paris on Wednesday, with the FIA expected to publish its decision after the proceedings. Qatar Grand Prix: F1 returns to action this weekend Formula 1 heads to Lusail from November 27 to 29 for the penultimate round of the 2026 season. The Qatar Grand Prix returns to the traditional weekend format, with three practice sessions, qualifying and Sunday’s race. The race will be particularly demanding on tyres. Pirelli has imposed a maximum of 27 laps per tyre set , meaning drivers will have to make at least two pit stops. Max Verstappen arrives as the winner of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, while the battle for second place in the Constructors’ Championship remains an important storyline heading into the final two rounds. records.excerpt: Photo: © IMAGO Change your timezone: Latest F1 News Max Verstappen's Qatar GP plans take hit as key ally Gianpiero Lambiase takes personal leave Lambiase forced to miss his penultimate race with Verstappen By Brian Van Hinthum . Friday 27 November 2026 08:15 Make us your Google favorite Gianpiero Lambiase will also be absent from the Red Bull pit wall during the Qatar Grand Prix this weekend. The regular race engineer for Max Verstappen is missing due to personal reasons, which means Tom Hart will once again handle radio communications, according to De Telegraaf . Originally, Lambiase was scheduled to oversee the final two race weekends of the season, in Qatar and at the season finale in Abu Dhabi on December 6th. Article continues under video After this year, the British-Italian engineer will leave Red Bull and begin a gardening leave period before taking on the role of chief racing officer at McLaren . Since May 2016, Lambiase and Verstappen formed a consistent partnership that yielded four world championships between 2021 and 2024. F1 HEADLINES: Hamilton's Ferrari power shift as FIA hold review to grand prix result Successor in place At the Milton Keynes team, the succession plan for next year is already set. Lambiase currently serves as Head of Racing, a position that Tom McCullough will take over starting in 2027 after transferring from Aston Martin. From that same year, Hart will officially become Verstappen’s full-time race engineer for every grand prix. Hart has been with Red Bull since 2013, initially working as a performance engineer for Verstappen starting in 2020. This season, he held a senior role supporting both team drivers. Due to this internal promotion, Hart rejected a previous offer to join Williams , choosing to continue his career at Red Bull. Tom Hart is Max Verstappen's new race engineer First win together To get accustomed to their new roles, Hart had already been on the pit wall for Verstappen during the Austin and Brazil races this season. Last weekend in Las Vegas, Verstappen secured the 75th Grand Prix win of his Formula 1 career, marking the first time Hart’s voice was heard on the radio during one of Verstappen’s victories. After the race in the US. gambling city, the stand-in engineer was visibly happy and even received a congratulatory pat on the shoulder from Jos Verstappen in the garage. Hart was scheduled to hand back the reins for the final two races to allow for a proper farewell to Lambiase, but with Lambiase’s unforeseen absence, Hart will continue in the role for the time being. records.excerpt: ‘What the f**k do they want?’ – Bortoleto slams drivers’ Las Vegas GP criticism Taylor Powling & Thomas Maher 26 Nov 2026 3:54 PM The Las Vegas GP produced a record number of overtakes Gabriel Bortoleto has lambasted the drivers who complained about the racing product in the Las Vegas Grand Prix, questioning ‘what the f**k do they want?’ in Formula 1. Last weekend’s race at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit proved to be a pulsating, action-packed spectacle, with a record-breaking 352 overtakes being made across the 50 laps. Bortoleto slams rivals after Las Vegas criticism That included 35 changes of lead as the emphasis on battery deployment, combined with long straights, allowed drivers to regain a place immediately after being passed. However, while several drivers revelled in the back-and-forth battles, others were less enthusiastic, most notably race winner Max Verstappen, who likened it to ‘Mario Kart’. When asked whether he enjoyed it, the Red Bull driver answered: “When I look at it from, like, my racer heart, not when you look at it as a show spectacle, yes. I enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart. “No, like, even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because, I don’t know, it’s just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably yes, you like it.” More from the Qatar GP Max Verstappen poised for final races with ‘GP’ before Red Bull exit Lando Norris hilariously roasts Ted Kravitz in Russell ‘prove it’ theory But while he has acknowledged that he wasn’t in the same boat as many of his rivals due to Audi’s top-speed deficit, Bortoleto has highlighted that the drivers are the first to complain when there are minimal overtaking opportunities during a race. “Look, for me, I must be honest that maybe because we struggle with the speed on the straights, I was always making overtakes at the last second in the middle of the corner. So for me it was actually quite nice,” he expressed. “Rarely, I made a few moves in the middle of the straight when the other car was running out of battery. But most of the moves I made… with Ollie, for example, were always in T1, super close battle. “I quite enjoyed the race, I must say, I wouldn’t complain about it. And I think at the same time, we need to give it a break. I think some drivers have been complaining when it’s not overtaking, when it’s overtaking, so what the f**k do they want? You need to drive and do your job.” Bortoleto, now coming to the end of his sophomore campaign in F1, admitted that it had been a while since he had encountered the type of racing that prevailed in Vegas. Pressed on whether he had to deploy unusual skills to adapt to the circumstances, the Brazilian retorted: “No, no. Again, it was normal overtaking for me. “It was actually very long that I didn’t have such close fights. “I finished the race, I went to talk with Ollie. It was super cool, how close the battle between us two was. Also with Nico, I had a few fights with him. “So, if something actually just bringing back a little bit that feeling of overtaking that for a few races we didn’t have.” Read next: Carlos Sainz lays bare daunting gap facing Williams after F1 2026 struggles Audi Gabriel Bortoleto

records.excerpt: F1 takes unprecedented action ahead of Qatar Grand Prix F1 takes unprecedented action ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Oliver Harden 27 Nov 2026 7:03 AM George Russell (Mercedes W16) leads a queue of cars at the start of the Qatar Grand Prix sprint race in 2025 The F1 2026 cars will be forced to run minimum front-tyre pressures of 29psi at this weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix, the FIA has confirmed. The move sets a new record for the highest minimum front-tyre pressures at the start of an F1 race weekend. FIA confirms 29psi minimum front-tyre pressures at Qatar Grand Prix The Lusail circuit in Qatar will host the penultimate race of the F1 2026 season this weekend. The high-energy circuit has proven demanding since it arrived on the calendar in 2021, when the race was marred by a series of late tyre failures. The FIA has taken a series of measures in the years since to guard against tyre problems, imposing a maximum tyre life of 18 laps per set in 2023 after issues were found with the circuit’s pyramid kerbs. A mandatory stint length of 25 laps was introduced for the Qatar Grand Prix in 2025, effectively forcing drivers to make two pit stops each. It was confirmed last week that a similar measure will be in place for 2026 , with the mandatory stint length increased to 27 laps. The hardest tyres in the Pirelli range – the C1, C2 and C3 compounds – will be used in Qatar this weekend to cope with the high lateral loads of the Lusail circuit. In a further move, the FIA’s competition notes – distributed to teams by race director Rui Marques on Thursday – confirmed that the minimum front tyre pressures will be set at 29psi in Qatar. It marks a new record for the highest minimum front-tyre pressures at the start of a Formula 1 race weekend. The previous benchmark for minimum front-tyre pressures in the F1 2026 season was 28psi, which was in place in Japan (Suzuka), Britain (Silverstone) and Belgium (Spa). Pirelli increased the minimum front-tyre pressures to 29psi in Qatar in 2025 after cuts were found in the tyres following Friday’s running. A minimum pressure of 28psi had been set at the start of the weekend. It remains to be seen whether the tyre pressures will be raised further still as the weekend unfolds. Meanwhile, the minimum rear tyre pressures in Qatar will be 27.5psi, slightly down on the 28psi in place at Spa and Las Vegas. The starting pressures for the rear tyres in Qatar are 4psi higher than in 2025, the last year under the previous ground-effect rules. Preview: Qatar Grand Prix 2026 Qatar GP predictions: Ferrari fireworks, awkward Russell and Verstappen, 400 overtakes FIA makes key decision ahead of Qatar Grand Prix In its Qatar Grand Prix preview, Pirelli explained that the lower levels of aerodynamic load produced by the F1 2026 cars have resulted in the increased mandatory stint length of 27 laps. The tyre manufacturer also noted that the absence of the sprint format, which limits practice running to a single hour on Friday, will help teams adapt to the unique challenge of Qatar. Pirelli said: “The track layout remains unchanged from last year and continues to provide a particularly severe test for the tyres, especially in terms of lateral loads and operating temperatures. “For this race, Pirelli has selected the three hardest compounds in its range: the C1 as Hard, the C2 as Medium, and the C3 as Soft. “The choice is dictated by the characteristics of the Qatari circuit, which generates a particularly high level of wear, especially on the front-left tyre. “The circuit features 16 corners and its high level of severity stems from the succession of high-speed turns, which subject the tyres to continuous stress for much of the lap. “The relatively smooth track surface and the high track temperatures can encourage graining on all compounds, a phenomenon that further increases wear. “Despite operating in very demanding conditions, the tyres deliver consistent performance throughout the stint. Experience from previous years has shown that performance degradation remains relatively limited even when wear levels are high. “To prevent tyres from being used beyond their intended life, managing degradation while placing excessive fatigue on the structure, Pirelli has introduced, in agreement with the FIA, a maximum stint length of 27 laps for each set. “As a result, the race will inevitably be a minimum two-stop event for all drivers. “The maximum lap limit has been increased compared to last year because the 2026 tyres feature a further reinforced construction and the cars generate lower levels of aerodynamic load than their 2025 predecessors. “The introduction of this restriction, as an alternative to other measures such as increasing minimum starting pressures, will allow drivers to push harder during their stints, reducing the need for pace management. “The absence of the Sprint format, which was in place last year, will also make life easier for the teams, both in managing the remaining mileage available on each tyre set and in fine-tuning their cars during free practice.” Read next: ‘Disgusts me’ – Former Toro Rosso driver calls out Max Verstappen over George Russell rivalry hypocrisy FIA Related Articles Oliver Harden 27 Nov 2026 FIA reaches Sergio Perez decision after Qatar GP press conference delay Sergio Perez's explanation has come to light. records.excerpt: Liam Lawson doubles down as FIA decision under further scrutiny Liam Lawson doubles down as FIA decision under fresh scrutiny Jamie Woodhouse & Thomas Maher 26 Nov 2026 6:51 PM Liam Lawson was one frustrated driver after Las Vegas Liam Lawson doubled down on his frustration over not being allowed to claw back more of his deficit after a Safety Car appearance in Las Vegas. While accepting the safety and race scenario aspects, Lawson suggested that what happened in Sin City defeats the purpose of the lapped cars may overtake ruling. Liam Lawson reflects on Las Vegas GP frustration Lawson began the race a lap down on the pack due to a pre-race fuel leak which required a rapid Racing Bulls repair job. Opportunity knocked when a collision between Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara brought out the Safety Car. However, having received the instruction, after four laps, to overtake the Safety Car, allowing him to regain the lead lap and chase down the back of the back of the field with the race neutralised, the race resumed when he still had a 20-second deficit to the rest of the field. “I don’t know why they took four laps to release me,” he had questioned after the race. Prior to the Qatar Grand Prix, Lawson further addressed his frustrations when speaking with PlanetF1.com and other accredited media. He was eventually classified 14th at the wheel of a Racing Bulls machine that, in the hands of Arvid Lindblad, ran in the top three places in the early stages. “It was so frustrating because I had no tow, like not a single car in sight. So as a driver, it’s really frustrating. “Especially in a race like Vegas. You’re not looking after tyres, you’re just flat out. So when you’re flat out, but you’re racing nobody and you’re a lap down, it’s a really mentally frustrating race. “I’m just watching the screens the whole time to watch the race to basically see what’s happening, praying for a Safety Car or something like that. Then we got the Safety Car and unfortunately didn’t have enough time to catch the field. So even more frustrating again to be on the lead lap, but still 25 seconds back. “So overall, it was just frustrating, and then to see the performance of the car afterwards as well, and see the pace that we had. Yeah, it was frustrating.” Having questioned the delay in being allowed to unlap himself in Vegas, Lawson was asked whether it was something that Racing Bulls has discussed with the FIA, or whether he will raise it in the drivers’ briefing discussions which take place ahead of each race. “I understand the safety aspect of it. I don’t want to compromise that at all,” he clarified. “But I just think when we have these double yellow zones anyway, I’m going to follow the delta in there and slow down regardless, so that zone won’t be any different. So as if I was following a Safety Car, and the rest of the lap, I could be catching back up. “I also understand that they need to get the race going when everybody’s struggling with tyre temps and stuff like that. So I think it was just bad timing. “But it kind of defeats the purpose a little bit when you get your lap back, but you don’t actually get your lap back.” Latest Qatar GP talking points on PlanetF1.com Charles Leclerc rejects Ferrari contract theory in unprecedented reveal Max Verstappen poised for final races with ‘GP’ before Red Bull exit Racing Bulls and Alpine have reached crunch time in the battle for fifth in the Constructors’ Championship. records.excerpt: Honda contradicts Fernando Alonso over cause of Las Vegas GP retirement Taylor Powling & Thomas Maher 26 Nov 2026 2:07 PM Fernando Alonso retired on the last lap of the Las Vegas GP Honda has admitted that it has been unable to diagnose any problems with the power unit in Fernando Alonso ’s Aston Martin , despite his claim to the contrary after his retirement from last weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Aston Martin’s disastrous debut campaign with Honda reached another low at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, as Alonso, having already contended that he was losing up to three seconds on the straights, slammed the race as the partnership’s “worst” of 2026. Honda and Fernando Alonso at odds over Las Vegas retirement The Spaniard had been circulating at the back around the power-sensitive track along with teammate Lance Stroll when he reported that his engine was “broken” before then pulling into the pits on the last lap to retire instead of taking the chequered flag. “We saw already in qualifying that the engine was down, and I think the race was the whole race down,” Alonso said after the Las Vegas GP. “So I was losing a lot of time on the straights, not only to the rest of the field, but also to Lance [Stroll]. I think in the last two laps, the engine completely gave up.” Following the race, though, Honda’s chief engineer, Shintaro Orihara, divulged that it had not spotted any anomalies on the data from the powertrain in Alonso ’s AMR26. And while it conducted more thorough checks in the subsequent days, Orihara reiterated that the Japanese marque has still not found anything to support Alonso’s claim. “We have checked all the data we have now, and also in the maintenance, we also checked the engine physically,” Orihara told PlanetF1.com and other accredited media. “At this moment, we haven’t found any issues with the engine from the data or from the maintenance. But we will check on Friday how the engine works on this track.” Orihara has emphasised that Honda will continue to value Alonso’s feedback, even though the two parties remain at odds over the reason for his retirement in Las Vegas. “We carefully analysed his comments, and we also respect his comments. That’s why we checked all the data, and we also checked the engine condition,” he said. “But from the data, at the moment we haven’t seen any issues. But again, as I mentioned, we should check again on Friday to get some feedback from Fernando.” More from the Qatar GP FIA makes key decision ahead of Qatar Grand Prix Qatar GP predictions: Ferrari fireworks, awkward Russell and Verstappen, 400 overtakes Orihara has suggested that Honda’s continued uncompetitiveness in 2026 – which was exacerbated on the 1.9-kilometre back straight along the Las Vegas Strip – might have contributed to Alonso’s intuition that there was something wrong with his power unit. “From the data viewpoint, we haven’t seen any issue,” he repeated. “Probably this year our engine performance is not enough to give confidence to [the] driver, and then probably they feel some feeling of engine performance is not great.” Honda introduced a measure last weekend to prevent a repeat of the battere failure that curtailed Lance Stroll’s race in Brazil ahead of a complete overhaul for next year. However, in the meantime, Orihara disclosed that another slight revision to improve reliability of the battery will potentially be introduced at the final round in Abu Dhabi. “In Las Vegas we brought some countermeasures for the battery issue,” he said. “We completed full race distance, maybe one lap less, but almost full distance without any issue. That is a positive sign. Still, we need to work to improve our reliability. “We may bring another countermeasure if we find a good solution. And again, as I mentioned, ’27, we have plans to update our inside structure to improve our reliability.” Read next: Haas complete 2027 F1 grid with confirmation of final driver signing Aston Martin Fernando Alonso Honda

Photo: © IMAGO Change your timezone: F1 News & Gossip Honda in race against time as shock F1 engine plan revealed Big changes are on the horizon Simmey Hannifin Donaldson F1 Editor Motorsport journalist covering F1 since 2024 Wednesday 25 November 2026 19:55 Make us your Google favorite After plenty of criticism surrounding the 2026 F1 power units, big changes are coming in the future, but it could be terrible news for Honda. The Japanese manufacturer currently supplies one team on the grid - Aston Martin - but has undoubtedly produced the weakest power unit of all five manufacturers this year, both in terms of pace and reliability. Las Vegas marked round 21 of the 2026 campaign, for example, but Fernando Alonso complained that the Honda power unit did not work as it should for every lap of the grand prix in Nevada before eventually retiring metres from the finish line due to a 'broken' engine. The previous race in Sao Paulo, Lance Stroll was forced to retire from his 13th grand prix of the season with the engine the culprit, as it so often has been this season. Article continues under video The FIA's latest ADUO analysis also confirmed that Honda remains in the worst group of engine manufacturers, more than four per cent behind the current benchmark, Red Bull. F1 HEADLINES: Verstappen trolls George Russell AGAIN as Mercedes hit by FIA rule change Honda could be running out of time That ADUO ruling means that Honda can make two additional upgrades to their power unit in 2027, with the manufacturer themselves under no illusions as to the work they have to do, with chief trackside engineer Shintaro Orihara having previously outlined their upgrade plans for 2027. Per Orihara, Honda are planning a major upgrade at the start of the 2027 season, but this will not be enough to get them to the front of the field when it comes to power units, with further upgrades then required to make that leap. The issue is, this week, F1 and the FIA confirmed that a unanimous agreement had been reached regarding the 2030 power unit, with the sport set to switch to a V8 engine that prioritises sustainable fuels and uses only limited hybrid technology - a big shift from the 2026 regulations. And, while that is four years away, The Race claim that, as a result of those changes on the horizon, F1's current engines will likely be frozen from mid-2028 onwards. This essentially means that Honda only has just over 18 months to solve their current power unit gremlins, and anything that is not remedied by that date would have to be carried for the remainder of that season and in 2029. For teams at the front of the grid whose power unit does not prevent them from being competitive, that's not a problem. However, with Honda still facing both performance and reliability issues, it puts an immense amount of pressure on them to get their upgrades right heading into 2027. The clock is ticking. records.title: Aston Martin in new admission after Stroll’s eye-opening Honda request
records.excerpt: Aston Martin in new admission after Stroll’s eye-opening Honda request Jamie Woodhouse 25 Nov 2026 10:09 AM Lance Stroll driving the Aston Martin AMR26 Both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll bemoaned a lack of straight-line performance from the Honda engine in Las Vegas, the latter requesting more horsepower to the tune of two seconds. But amid that scrutiny on Honda, Aston Martin faces an important test of where its AMR26 chassis is at as the Qatar Grand Prix looms. Chief trackside officer Mike Krack believes there is also performance to find on the team’s side, and the Lusail International Circuit will highlight the AMR26’s performance level through high-speed corners. Aston Martin will get AMR26 answer in Qatar Despite progress being made, the F1 2026 Honda power unit continues to suffer from a lack of grunt compared to rival creations. This was vividly on show at the high-speed Las Vegas Strip Circuit. The Aston Martins were cut adrift with Cadillac during qualifying, while Stroll brought the sole surviving AMR26 home in P17, after Alonso was forced to retire with an engine issue near the end. Alonso believed that the deficit down the Las Vegas straights was potentially as extreme as three seconds. He heaped praise on the Aston Martin chassis for allowing him to claw back time through the corners. Stroll made the eye-opening claim of: “We have got to find like two seconds in a straight line, so Honda needs to find some horsepower.” The Canadian was subsequently asked whether he is confident that Honda is up to this task. “I don’t know,” was his response. With Honda put in the spotlight, Krack was asked after the Las Vegas GP whether Aston Martin still needs to make progress on the car side as well. “I think we certainly do have still some performance to find,” he confirmed. “I think we have seen when the speeds are low or when the grip is low, like in rain conditions or like in Sepang when it was very rough, that the car is strong in low speed. I think it’s fair to say that mainly in low speed it has a strength. “In high speed, we will see next week [in Qatar], because there is potentially only high-speed corners, so I think we will have a good answer there. “But I think it is clear, I think also after Budapest I said the upgrades have worked, that is very, very clear. But there is still a lot to work on. “I mean, we do circuit by circuit all the analysis in each type of corners. That is why I can say confidently that the car is a good step with low speed and that it is strong there, especially with the lower the grip. “But I think in medium and higher speed corners, we will have a good answer next week.” On the plus side for Honda, Stroll made it to the chequered flag in Las Vegas, overcoming his recent misfortune with battery issues. Honda’s chief engineer Shintaro Orihara was asked whether the manufacturer uncovered any new clues on its PU performance and energy management around this unique circuit. “This track is similar to Baku, but always small different things give us some ideas. “Also, we gathered interesting data from qualifying. “This track is challenging for us in terms of performance and energy management, and difficult to optimise or to follow ahead of cars. But still, we gathered some data, and that helps our development for next year.” Latest Aston Martin news on PlanetF1.com Lance Stroll submits eye-opening Honda request after Las Vegas GP ‘Typical Fernando Alonso’ – Aston Martin boss reacts to Dakar Rally confirmation Orihara also confirmed that Honda “performed some testing” in Las Vegas on its new countermeasures to address the recent battery issues. “We saw some positive things from the countermeasures,” he confirmed, but added: “I believe we need another step to get better reliability. “The positive thing is we completed a full race distance. But again, we need to understand the full picture of the battery issue, and still we need some countermeasures for next year.” Read next: Oliver Bearman criticises ‘joke’ Las Vegas GP situation as deliberate tactic revealed Aston Martin Fernando Alonso Honda Lance Stroll

records.title: Alonso misses Qatar GP media day with virus as Aston Martin plans Friday return
records.excerpt: Fernando Alonso will miss the Qatar Grand Prix’s Thursday media activities while recovering from a viral infection contracted during the Las Vegas weekend. Aston Martin expects the two-time Formula 1 world champion to arrive at Lusail on Friday, when he is scheduled to drive during the second free-practice session News Summary Alonso is absent from Thursday’s Qatar media commitments because of a viral infection. Aston Martin expects him back in the paddock on Friday, but has not confirmed fresh medical clearance for the rest of the weekend. Jak Crawford’s FP1 appearance was arranged before the illness and is not an emergency substitution. Fernando Alonso has been forced to miss the opening media activities of the Qatar Grand Prix after Aston Martin confirmed that he contracted a viral infection towards the end of the Las Vegas race weekend. The Spaniard will remain away from Thursday’s paddock commitments while recovering. Aston Martin has not announced a replacement for the Grand Prix or any alteration to its planned race line-up. Alonso will not be in the Qatar paddock for media day (Photo: Aston Martin) “Fernando will miss media day today as he continues to recover from a viral infection contracted towards the end of the Las Vegas GP weekend,” Aston Martin announced. “He is recovering well, and is planned to return to the paddock on Friday.” Why Crawford will drive Alonso’s car in FP1 Aston Martin had already selected American reserve driver Jak Crawford to take Alonso’s AMR26 for the opening practice session on Friday. The arrangement forms part of the team’s development programme and was confirmed before Alonso’s illness became public . Crawford was also scheduled for FP1 at Las Vegas, but rain severely limited running. The team therefore confirmed another outing for the American at Lusail . Crawford will drive in FP1 as part of the Aston Martin development programme (Photo: Aston Martin) The arrangement means Alonso was not due to drive in FP1 even if fully fit. His first planned on-track appearance remains FP2, subject to his recovery and the team’s assessment. Las Vegas difficulties precede Qatar weekend Alonso’s absence comes after a demanding Las Vegas race in which Aston Martin struggled with straight-line performance. The Spaniard retired late in the Grand Prix, a nd concerns over the Honda power unit have continued to dominate the team’s preparations . The two-time champion recently criticised Aston Martin’s straight-line deficit , pointing to the difficulties of recovering time lost on long acceleration zones. Qatar’s fast corners create a different challenge, requiring consistent tyre management and stability through long loaded sequences. The team will also use the weekend to gather information ahead of the final race in Abu Dhabi. Friday’s FP1 is scheduled for 16:30 local time, followed by FP2 at 20:00. The full Qatar schedule for six international markets includes practice, qualifying and Sunday’s race. GRANDE PRÊMIO is following the Qatar weekend with news, results and analysis in its Formula 1 coverage . FAQ Why is Alonso missing Qatar media day? Aston Martin confirmed he is recovering from a viral infection contracted at Las Vegas. Will Alonso race in Qatar? The team expects his return on Friday but has not announced his withdrawal from the race. Who drives Alonso’s car in FP1? Jak Crawford, in a previously scheduled young-driver appearance.

records.excerpt: Aston Martin issues Fernando Alonso statement ahead of Qatar GP Aston Martin issues Fernando Alonso statement ahead of Qatar GP Michelle Foster 26 Nov 2026 11:24 AM Fernando Alonso will miss Thursday's media day in Qatar Fernando Alonso will not attend Thursday’s media at the Qatar Grand Prix after falling ill during the Las Vegas GP weekend. Aston Martin says the Spaniard is “planned” to return to the paddock on Friday. Fernando Alonso will miss Thursday’s media day in Qatar Alonso qualified 19th in Sin City but retired from the Grand Prix due to an issue with his Honda engine. Aston Martin announced earlier this week that Alonso would miss FP1 at the Qatar Grand Prix, with Jak Crawford replacing him for the session after heavy rain washed out the American’s FP1 in Las Vegas. The team confirmed it would try again in Qatar, with Crawford jumping into Alonso’s AMR26 for FP1 around the Lusail International Circuit. It means Alonso has a bit more time to recover after contracting a virus during the Las Vegas weekend. Aston Martin announced on Thursday morning that the Spaniard would not attend Thursday’s media day at the Lusail circuit due to illness. The team said in a brief statement: “Fernando will miss media day today as he continues to recover from a viral infection contracted towards the end of the Las Vegas GP weekend. “He is recovering well, and is planned to return to the paddock on Friday.” F1 2026: The season’s winners and losers The results of the F1 2026 championship The F1 2026 Drivers’ and Constructors’ Championship standings Alonso confirmed last month that he would continue with Aston Martin next season, putting an end to speculation about his Formula 1 future. Shortly after, he also announced that he would contest the 2027 Dakar Rally, driving an Aston Martin Dreadnought. Alonso will form part of a three-car team along with nine-time World Rally Champion Sebastien Loeb and reigning world rally raid champion Lucas Moraes. Asked if his Dakar participation was something he had been thinking about in case he did decide to quit Formula 1, he simply replied: “Yes.” The Spaniard revealed that talks about him possibly signing up for the 2027 Dakar began at the British Grand Prix when he was approached by Prodrive’s David Richards. “No, it didn’t change,” he said. “I mean, Dakar was in my mind. Le Mans is in my mind. Indy 500 is in my mind. “I love competing. I love competing in race cars that you go on throttle and you have power. You go and brake and you have deceleration. We miss now in Formula One, so I was thinking that. “Then, obviously, if I continued in Formula One, that will be always my priority, and it’s difficult to put things together with different programmes. “Dakar, because it’s in January, it fit a little bit better, but then you know it had to come with a few coincidences as well. I think that was probably back in July. I think David Richards came to probably the Silverstone race, and it was that that conversation happened, you know. “But it was not even Aston involved; it was just with Prodrive. So I said, ‘I don’t know, David, I don’t know what is going to happen next year’. “I think things came into place quickly and happy and ready to learn as much as possible.” Read next: Qatar GP predictions: Ferrari fireworks, awkward Russell and Verstappen, 400 overtakes Aston Martin Fernando Alonso Related Articles Taylor Powling & Thomas Maher 26 Nov 2026 Honda contradicts Fernando Alonso over cause of Las Vegas GP retirement Fernando Alonso had claimed that he retired from the Las Vegas GP due to a Honda engine issue. records.excerpt: Fernando Alonso says Honda's engine performance and reliability problems are preventing Aston Martin from competing in Formula 1. F1 News Trending now Alonso says Honda engine leaves Aston Martin unable to compete By Gary Gowers Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro. Published 25 Nov 2026, 16:03 Follow on Google News Fernando Alonso says Aston Martin cannot be competitive with their current Honda power unit despite improvements to the team’s chassis. The two-time world champion has identified engine performance and reliability as the principal problems behind their disappointing Formula 1 campaign. Aston Martin have scored seven points from 21 races and sit 10th in the constructors’ championship. Alonso retired on the final lap of Sunday’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, while team-mate Lance Stroll finished 17th. Advertisement Alonso highlights Honda performance deficit Speaking to Aston Martin’s official website, Alonso said the team’s lack of straight-line speed had become particularly apparent at circuits such as Las Vegas, where he estimated they were losing more than two seconds per lap on the straights alone. “We can’t be competitive with the power unit we have,” the Spaniard said. He also expressed concern over reliability but acknowledged Honda’s efforts to address the problems. Advertisement The Japanese manufacturer introduced an engine upgrade at the Dutch Grand Prix, but difficulties have persisted during the second half of the season. Alonso stopped shortly before completing the race in Las Vegas after suspecting a power-unit problem. Honda are examining the circumstances surrounding his retirement. Chassis development encourages Alonso Despite his criticism of Honda, Alonso remains optimistic about the progress Aston Martin have made with their chassis. An upgrade introduced at the Hungarian Grand Prix delivered the performance improvements the team had anticipated. Alonso subsequently scored points in the Netherlands and Malaysia, where the circuit characteristics and conditions placed less emphasis on outright engine performance. The 45-year-old believes Aston Martin’s ability to move closer to the midfield following limited chassis development demonstrates the potential of the car. He also remains confident Honda can make progress before next season. Aston Martin seek improvement in Qatar Aston Martin have two opportunities remaining to add to their points total before the end of a difficult first season with Honda as their works engine partner. This weekend’s Qatar Grand Prix will provide another test of the team’s performance, with the high-speed corners at Lusail offering a contrast to the long straights of Las Vegas. For Alonso, the development of Honda’s power unit during the winter will be crucial to Aston Martin’s prospects of becoming more competitive in 2027. records.title: Aston Martin announce Qatar FP1 reshuffle
records.excerpt:
Fernando Alonso will sit out Free Practice 1 for Aston Martin to make way for Jak Crawford at the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix.

The 21-year-old will run his eighth FP1 session with the Silverstone-based team at the Lusail International Circuit this weekend.

Crawford will replace Alonso during the opening practice session on Friday, taking the wheel of the AMR26, one week on from a curtailed outing at Las Vegas.

Friday running at Vegas had seen treacherous conditions out on track after a rain shower. This meant no driver set a representative time, and Crawford himself only completed one installation lap for Aston Martin.

"We're pleased to share that Jak Crawford will be back in the AMR26 for FP1 at this weekend's Qatar GP," the team said.

"Following his limited running in Las Vegas last weekend, Jak will drive Fernando's car for the session."

The American racing driver has also driven the car for Aston Martin at Suzuka, the Red Bull Ring, Spa-Francorchamps, and the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez this season.

records.excerpt: パドックに衝撃。FIA F3王者ウーゴ・ウゴチュクウがFIA F2デビュー戦でポールポジション獲得。スレイター痛恨のスピンも9番手／F第13戦ルサイル予選 11/28(土) 1:07 配信 2026年FIA F2第13戦ルサイル ウーゴ・ウゴチュクウ（VAR）（Getty Images） 現地時間11月27日（金）、2026年FIA F2第13戦の予選がカタールのルサイル・インターナショナル・サーキットで行われ、今回がFIA F2デビュー戦のウーゴ・ウゴチュクウ（VAR）が最速タイムを記録。スポット参戦ながら、29日（日）に行われるフィーチャーレースのポールポジションを獲得し、F1カタールGPのパドックに衝撃が走った。 【写真】FIA F2デビュー戦でポールポジションを獲得したウーゴ・ウゴチュクウ（VAR） 宮田莉朋（ハイテック／TGR-DC）は11番手となった。 30分間の予選はF1のフリー走行1回目（FP1）終了直後、日本時間24時（現地時間18時）より開催された。セッション開始時点で、気温は25度、路面温度は30度、湿度は65パーセントだった。 アウトラップ、ウォームラップを経て計時上3周目に各車最初のアタックに臨んだ。そんななか、セクター1を35.6秒、セクター2を32.3秒という区間ベストタイムで駆け抜けたのは今回がFIA F2デビュー戦のフレディ・スレイター（インビクタ・レーシング／アウディ育成／2026年FIA F3選手権2位）だった。 最初のアタックで1分37秒162を刻んだスレイターは暫定首位につける。さらに、同じく今回がFIA F2デビュー戦のウゴチュクウ（2026年FIA F3王者）も暫定6番手という好タイムを刻んだ。 1周のクールダウンを経て、計時上5周目に各車2度目のアタックに入ると、スレイターが1分36秒446までタイムを縮めて暫定首位をキープ。さらにウゴチュクウが0.167秒差の暫定2番手に続き、今季のFIA F3王者と選手権2位が、FIA F2初戦でもワンツーを形成する状況となった。 決して、この時点でそのほかの車両が余力を残していたわけでもない。事実、フリー走行最速だったマルティニウス・ステンスホーン（ロダン・モータースポーツ）は悪くない走りで2アタック目をまとめた。しかし、それでもスレイターに0.289秒届かず暫定3番手だった。 セッション前半を終え、全車がピットに戻った時点で、スレイター、ウゴチュクウ、ステンスホーンに続く暫定4番手はラファエル・ヴィラゴメス（VAR）、暫定5番手はジョシュア・デュルクセン（インビクタ・レーシング／メルセデスF1開発ドライバー）だった。 残り時間10分ごろより各車は再びコースに入った。この時点でタイトル候補のニコラ・ツォロフ（カンポス・レーシング／レッドブル育成）はトラックリミット違反によるタイム抹消もあり暫定15番手、アレクサンダー・ダン（ロダン・モータースポーツ／アルピーヌ育成）は暫定6番手という状況だった。 ウォームアップラップを終え6台ほどがアタックに入ったころ、アウトラップ走行中のセバスチャン・モントーヤ（ダムス・ルーカスオイル）の右タイヤホイールが脱落し、コース上を転がる事態に。これでモントーヤはコースサイドでクルマを降り、チーム移籍後最初の予選を終えた。 モントーヤのストップで予選は残り5分37秒で赤旗中断に。なお、モントーヤの車両から金属らしきものが飛ぶシーンが国際映像のリプレイに登場している。また、クルマを降りたモントーヤはタイヤホイールを回収し、自らの手で転がしながらコースを離れている。 6分ほどの中断を経て予選セッションは再開された。残り時間がわずかだったこともあり、最大でも2アタックが限界だった。そんななか、ランキング4位のガブリエレ・ミニ（MPモータースポーツ／アルピーヌ育成）が1分35秒862を刻み暫定首位に浮上する。 ただ、その直後にウゴチュクウが1分35秒818を叩き出し、0.044秒差でミニから首位の座を奪った。一方、スレイターはセクター2で全体ベストを更新も、セクター3のターン12でオーバーシュートし、痛恨のスピンを喫してしまった。 さらにウゴチュクウは翌周にもアタックを敢行し、セクター1で全体ベストを更新していた。ただ、チームメイトのヴィラゴメスがセクター3でストップし、残り時間18秒で予選は2度目の赤旗に。この時点でセッション終了となった。 2026年FIA F3王者で、来季は強豪カンポス・レーシングからFIA F2フル参戦が決定しているウゴチュクウ。今回は経験を積むためにVARからのスポット参戦という状況だったが、FIA F2デビュー戦でポールポジションを獲得する大仕事を成し遂げた。0.044秒差の2番手はミニ、0.151秒差の3番手にダンと、タイトル獲得の可能性を残すふたりが続いた。 ツォロフはタイム更新も7番手、スレイターはミスが響くも9番手、フリー走行最速だったステンスホーンは10番手だった。
